1004: Built around Magnus the Red, dense bricks of Rubric Marines and Scarab Occult Terminators, Sorcerers buffing from inside Rhinos, a Winged Daemon Prince, and swarms of Tzaangors and Chaos Spawn, this is a layered psychic horde that floods the board with bodies while elite units deliver punishment. Grand Coven's rotating command-phase abilities — particularly Imbued Manifestation extending psychic ranged weapons and Psychic Maelstrom's trigger — let the army flip between reach and lethality turn by turn, with Eldritch Vortex of E'Taph and Umbralefic Crystal enhancing key characters to amplify that engine. It punishes low-model-count armies that cannot match the board presence, burying them under screening Spawn, objective-holding Tzaangors, and Rhino-delivered Rubrics while Magnus and the Daemon Prince apply elite pressure. Armies with reliable mortal-wound denial, strong anti-horde volume, or the ability to isolate and delete Magnus early crack this list open, since losing the central damage dealer collapses the lethality the board-control framework depends on.
1009: Built around Lords of Change, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Screamers, Tzaangors, and Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, this Changehost of Deceit list plays a layered, shape-shifting game where the Daemonic Illusions aura grants a 4+ invulnerable save against ranged attacks to any Scintillating Legions unit sitting within 6" of a Thousand Sons Psyker, turning the entire midfield into a resilient wall of protected bodies. The plan is to flood objectives with expendable Tzaangor screens and durable Rubric blobs while Lords of Change and Enlightened apply consistent ranged pressure and Scarab Occult Terminators punch into anything that contests. This build punishes attrition-focused shooting armies hard — layering the invulnerable aura across multiple units simultaneously makes straightforward anti-infantry overload largely ineffective. However, melee-heavy lists that can close quickly and break psyker coherence collapse the aura bubbles the moment they isolate the supporting casters.
1012: Built around Allarus Custodians, Vertus Praetors, Custodian Wardens, Prosecutors, Witchseekers, and Shield-Captains on Dawneagle Jetbikes, this Lions of the Emperor list lives and dies by its detachment rule: spread your elite units apart so each fights in isolation, gaining +1 to hit and +1 to wound on every attack. The win condition is surgical — isolate individual units across multiple objectives, trigger the detachment bonus on each combat independently, and grind opponents down through layered, high-quality attacks rather than a single concentrated kill spike. It punishes mid-density armies that cannot match the board coverage of fast jetbikes and deep-striking Allarus, leaving threats stranded outside support range. The weakness is coordination — opponents who can collapse spacing with aggressive screens or deny isolation zones through terrain and bubble-wrap force the detachment bonus offline, suddenly making elite Custodes points look very steep.
1013: Built around Custodian Guard, Blade Champions, Custodian Wardens, Contemptor-Achillus Dreadnoughts, Venatari Custodians, and Vertus Praetors under the Might of the Moritoi detachment, this is a full-spectrum mobile toolbox that pushes every unit type — infantry, walkers, and bikes — up the board faster through the detachment's +2" Movement and charge roll bonuses. The win condition is aggressive board presence: threatening charges from multiple vectors simultaneously to force bad trades, while Shield Host's Martial Ka'tah cycling swings between Critical Hit fishing and AP improvement to adapt the kill chain to whatever needs removing. It punishes slow, static armies that cannot contest midfield early, as the mobility advantage lets Custodes establish primary control before the opponent stabilises a gunline. It cracks open against high-volume mortal wound output or elite-killing shooting that can strip key pieces before they close — fewer, more expensive bodies means each casualty hits disproportionately hard.
1014: Built around Allarus Custodians, Witchseekers, Vertus Praetors, Custodian Wardens, and Prosecutors, this is a mobile, layered elite force that floods multiple threat vectors simultaneously rather than committing to a single delivery system. The engine runs on Allarus dropping via ingress to threaten charges, Vertus Praetors pressuring flanks, and Anathema Psykana units — Witchseekers and Prosecutors — advancing while remaining action-eligible, keeping primary score ticking without sacrificing board presence. It punishes slow, static armies by surrounding them with overlapping elite threats, forcing inefficient trades across multiple fronts where every Custodes model removed costs the opponent disproportionate resources. It cracks against fast alpha-strike lists that can strip the Allarus before they charge and collapse the Anathema Psykana screening layer before it establishes action tempo.
1019: Built around Allarus Custodians and a Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator Armour as the hammer, Vertus Praetors and Venatari Custodians as the mobile threat, and Custodian Guard, Wardens, Prosecutors, Witchseekers, and a Blade Champion filling out a layered board presence, this list runs Shield Host with Tharanatoi Hammerblow providing Allarus re-rolls on charge after an ingress move. The win condition is multi-angle pressure: Allarus deep strike in, ingress into position, then re-roll their charge to crack priority targets while jetbikes and Venatari contest and score around them. It punishes slower, castle-style armies that can't peel threats from multiple vectors simultaneously, leveraging Ka'tah's rotating buffs to stay relevant across different combat phases. It cracks open against lists that can deny or punish the ingress timing, stripping the Allarus of their charge re-roll and leaving expensive models exposed in the open.
1023: Built around Lords on Juggernauts, Flesh Hounds, Bloodletters, Jakhals, Goremongers, Slaughterbound, Exalted Eightbound, Skarbrand, Khorne Berzerkers, Forgefiends, and a Daemon Prince, this is a Khorne Daemonkin mass-horde brawler that layers daemons and mortals into a mobile wall of bodies. The engine is the Blood Tithe Point economy — every destroyed enemy unit fishing for a 3+ BTP roll funds mid-game power spikes, while Vessels of Wrath lets Characters punch with Cleave 1 or improved AP to crack armour in melee. It punishes elite low-model-count lists through sheer volume of threats, forcing opponents into uncomfortable trade sequences where killing anything fuels the BTP engine. It struggles against armies that can strip its screening layers at range before the charge, denying the kill-chain that generates BTP in the first place.
427: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Crisis Sunforges, Starscythes, Fireknives, Coldstar and Enforcer Commanders, Commander Farsight, the Twin Lance, and Pathfinders screening with Kroot Carnivores, this is a mobile battlesuit swarm running Experimental Prototype Cadre — extending Battlesuit Character range by 6" — and layering in Kauyon's Sustained Hits 1 and modifier-ignoring Guided attacks from round three onward. The plan is to control mid-table with durable battlesuit bricks, use Pathfinders to Spot targets for the Greater Good Guided chains, then unleash a sustained-fire kill spike in the late game to clear objectives by force. It punishes static gunlines and lightly screened elite armies that can't contest the mid-table early, since Crisis variants overload anti-armour priority while Coldstars reposition freely to exploit gaps. It struggles against aggressive alpha-strike lists that can shatter the battlesuit bricks before Kauyon activates, leaving the late-game damage engine without its key enablers.
430: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Kâhl, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and the Hekaton Land Fortress under the Hearthguard Covenant detachment, this list plays a dense mid-board infantry brawl backed by serious firepower, with Hernkyn Pioneers, Sagitaurs, and Kapricus Carriers keeping units mobile and threatening across the table. The core engine is punishing close-range engagements — Hearthguard Covenant lets Kâhls, Ûthar, and Hearthguard re-roll wound rolls of 1 on ranged attacks within 9", so the list advances aggressively to collapse that gap and then unloads into whatever it's touching, with Thunderkyn providing midfield fire support and Needgaârd Oathband (in nearly two-thirds of lists) banking YP every time it kills a unit. It punishes low-model-count elite armies brutally, as the combination of wound re-rolls at close range and high-damage shooting from Thunderkyn and the Land Fortress makes expensive enemy units disappear fast. Extended gunline armies that keep the Hearthguard outside 9" deny the re-roll and can chip this list apart before it closes the distance.
436: Built around Poxwalkers, Deathshroud Terminators, Myphitic Blight-Haulers, Foetid Bloat-Drones, a Lord of Contagion, Lord of Virulence, and Tallyman, the Contagion Engines detachment grants every Bloat-Drone and Blight-Hauler the Assault rule on their ranged weapons, turning the entire mechanised swarm into a mobile, shoot-and-charge pressure machine. The win condition is layered attrition: flood the midboard with Poxwalkers to spread Contagion and Afflict enemies, then drive Blight-Haulers and Bloat-Drones into range to delete infantry and armour alike while Deathshroud and the Lord of Contagion clean up in melee. It punishes slow, low-output lists that cannot deal with simultaneous threats across multiple vectors — Contagion chip damage stacks while the mechanised core tears through armoured targets with mobile anti-tank firepower. Elite, high-damage alpha-strike armies that can drop the Bloat-Drones and Blight-Haulers before Contagion scales crack this list open, since the engine collapses quickly without its vehicles applying pressure.
438: Built around Kastelan Robots paired with Cybernetica Datamsmiths, Belisarius Cawl, Skitarii Rangers, and Tech-Priest Enginseers, this list runs two detachments simultaneously — Lords of the Forge granting Tech-Priests a 4+/5+ FNP defensive stack and the Baffling Data Screed harassment ability, plus Cohort Cybernetica adding 2" Move and +1 OC to Legio Cybernetica units. The plan is to push fat, high-OC Kastelan blobs into the midboard, contest objectives with inflated Objective Control, and grind opponents out through layered durability while Rangers and Infiltrators screen flanks and deny easy scoring. It punishes slower gunlines and infantry hordes that can't generate enough anti-vehicle volume to chew through multiple tough Kastelan bricks before the clock runs out. Armies that can generate concentrated high-damage alpha strikes or strong melee threats into the midboard can crack the formation before its OC advantage becomes insurmountable, and the list's mediocre ranged output means it rarely wins by killing first.
446: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Captain with Jump Pack, Sanguinary Priest, Commander Dante, and Bladeguard Veterans screened by Scouts and Intercessors, the Liberator Assault Group is a wall-to-wall jump infantry assault force running the eponymous detachment's charge bonus — +2 Strength and +1 Attack on every melee weapon after a charge. The plan is to crash multiple buffed units into combat simultaneously, with the Sanguinary Priest sustaining the Sanguinary Guard and the Captain stacking command auras to create kill-chains that delete key targets and score through supremacy rather than passive holding. It punishes slow, dense infantry lists that cannot screen every angle, because the sheer volume of high-Strength swings after a charge overwhelms toughness thresholds across multiple units in one phase. Armies with strong shooting, deep-strike denial, and durable backline screens crack it open by stalling the charge engine before it connects.
447:
Built around Chosen, Cultist Mob, Abaddon the Despoiler, Masters of the Maelstrom, and Red Corsairs Raiders, this is a mass-horde pressure list running Cabal of Chaos with Fellhammer Siege-host as its dominant defensive layer — flooding the table with bodies while Abaddon and elite Chosen hit hard up the middle.

The plan is to drown opponents in chaff screens, use Dark Pact-boosted Chosen to spike Strength on key shooting targets, and let Abaddon bully melee priority threats while Masters of the Maelstrom keeps the engine running with command-phase utility.

Fellhammer's wound-roll penalty punishes armies leaning on high-Strength shooting to crack mid-Toughness infantry, making attrition wars deeply unfavorable for opponents expecting clean trades.

Low model durability per elite unit and Dark Pact's inherent risk mean a disciplined alpha strike that isolates Abaddon early or strips cultist screens before they screen can collapse the entire structure.
448: Built around Defilers, Cultist Mobs, and Warpsmiths, this list pairs daemon engines with cheap screening bodies and mechanical support to project armour and board presence simultaneously. The plan is to grind forward using Defilers as mobile anti-armour and mid-table brawlers while Cultists contest objectives cheaply, with Warpsmiths keeping the engines operational and threatening; scoring comes through sustained presence rather than explosive turns. It punishes opponent lists that rely on high-Strength, high-volume shooting to clear vehicles, since the sheer number of Defilers forces anti-tank overload decisions while Cultist chaff absorbs incidental fire. However, it struggles against precision elite melee threats that can isolate and delete individual Defilers before the Warpsmith support matters, leaving the list's scoring base suddenly exposed.
450:
Built around Lady Malys, Drazhar, Lelith Hesperax, Wyches, Incubi, and a swarm of Venoms and Raiders, this list is a mass-horde skimmer force that floods the board with fast, transported infantry across nearly every slot.

The plan is to use layered lethality from multiple elite melee threats simultaneously — Drazhar and Incubi cracking armoured targets while Lelith and Wyches overwhelm chaff — cycling units out of transports to control primary and force favourable trades every turn.

It punishes lists that struggle to clear volume efficiently, since the sheer number of bodies across Venoms, Raiders, and Wych mobs makes it nearly impossible to table before the melee threats arrive.

However, high-volume shooting armies that can strip transports early and strand infantry in the open crack this build apart, as the glass-cannon infantry lose most of their threat without the mobility and protection of their skimmers.
451: Built around Venoms, Raiders, Archons leading Incubi, Drazhar, Lady Malys, Wyches, Mandrakes, Reavers, and Scourges with heavy weapons, this is a swarming skimmer fleet that floods the table with fast transports, elite melee packets, and cheap board-control infantry simultaneously. The win condition is layered attrition and objective bleed — Venoms and Scourges whittle exposed units from range while Incubi and Drazhar disembark to butcher priority targets in melee, with Lady Malys providing command flexibility and Hand of the Archon locking down mid-board objectives. It punishes slow, static armies that can't answer simultaneous threats across multiple vectors, as the sheer volume of skimmer mobility and cheap screening bodies overwhelms piecemeal gunlines. It cracks apart against armies that can reliably strip transports before the melee payload deploys or that bring enough high-volume firepower to chew through the horde faster than it can score.
455: Built around Nekrosor Ammentar, Skorpekh Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Lokhust Lords, Lokhust Destroyers, Skorpekh Lords, the Void Dragon, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, Lychguard, Flayed Ones, and Imotekh, this is a Cursed Legion force that runs an overwhelming toolbox of Destroyer Cult units supercharged by a permanent +2 Strength buff — and a snowballing additional +2 whenever they kill or cripple something. The win condition is a kill-chain cascade: each destroyed or halved unit triggers the strength bonus, letting subsequent Destroyer units punch through armour saves they'd otherwise bounce off, while Ophydian and Flayed Ones pressure objectives from unexpected angles. It punishes static elite armies that cluster expensive models, because the strength-stacking kill chain turns single kills into multi-unit collapses in one activation window. Spread-out MSU lists that deny clean first kills can stall the cascade before it ignites, leaving the Destroyers fighting at base output against screens they can't efficiently clear.
456: Built around Canoptek Wraiths, Technomancers, Canoptek Doomstalkers, Canoptek Reanimators, Illuminor Szeras, Canoptek Scarab Swarms, and the Void Dragon, this is a highly mobile, self-sustaining Canoptek Court list that keeps its entire army within the Power Matrix by contesting objectives across the board from turn one. The plan is to flood No Man's Land with fast Wraiths and Scarab screens, lock down enough objective markers to extend the Power Matrix mid-board, then use Reanimators and Technomancers to keep key pieces cycling back while Doomstalkers apply consistent mid-range firepower. It punishes slow, static gunlines that can't clear durable, constantly-resurrecting units fast enough to deny the objective control that fuels the Power Matrix engine. However, elite alpha-strike lists or high-volume mortal-wound output that can delete pieces before the repair loop kicks in will crack this build wide open, as the resurrection chain relies on units surviving the initial engagement.
465: Built around Defilers, Daemonettes, Infractors, Lords Exultant, Tormentors, and Chaos Rhinos, this list runs the Carnival of Excess detachment — pairing Emperor's Children and Legions of Excess units to keep everything Empowered and pumping Sustained Hits — with three-quarters of lists adding Frenzied Host's advance-then-strike +1 Strength bonus on Battleline units. The plan is to flood the mid-table with Rhino-delivered Infractors and waves of Daemonettes, using Lords Exultant to stack Empowered auras while Defilers threaten armour and force awkward priority splits. It punishes static gunlines and low-volume elite forces that can't chew through layered chaff before the close-combat threat arrives in their face. It cracks against high-lethality alpha-strike lists that can strip Rhinos before disembarkation and collapse the Empowered bubble before it generates value.
466: Built around Flawless Blades, Tormentors, Lord Exultants, Infractors, Noise Marines, Lucius, Fulgrim, and Lord Kakophonists — with Chaos Rhinos ferrying the infantry forward — this is a Court of the Phoenician assault army that weaponises the Sensational Performance charge bonus to crash into fresh targets every fight phase rather than grinding the same unit twice. The win condition is a coordinated mid-table brawl: Rhinos deliver Flawless Blades and Infractors into charges, Sensational Performance forces them onto new targets each activation, and Lords Exultant amplify the kill chain while Fulgrim and Lucius punch out priority threats. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot absorb the volume of charge attacks landing on multiple units simultaneously each turn. It struggles against shooting-heavy lists that can strip Rhinos before the charge lands and against screens deep enough to blunt Sensational Performance by denying clean multi-unit charge lanes.
467: Built around Intercessor Squads, Scout Squads, Incursors, Bladeguard Veterans, Victrix Honour Guard with Marneus Calgar, and Repulsor Executioners, this Ceramite Sentinels list plants itself in terrain and grinds — every Adeptus Astartes unit inside a feature re-rolls hit and wound rolls of 1, and gains the Entrenched keyword, making garrisoned units extremely difficult to dislodge. The win condition is controlling terrain early with cheap infantry screens while Repulsor Executioners pour sustained heavy fire downfield, letting Calgar and the Honour Guard anchor central objectives against all comers. It punishes aggressive, close-range armies that have to charge into entrenched positions, absorbing attacks and returning fire with hit-and-wound re-rolls already active. It struggles against mobile shooting armies that can threaten its vehicles from range before it settles, or lists with strong deep-strike pressure that bypass its defensive terrain bubble entirely.
468: Built around Vulkan He'stan, multiple Infernus Squads, Land Raider Redeemers, and a Librarian-heavy support core, this list runs a close-range fire army where every Adeptus Astartes ranged weapon gains Assault and +1 Strength within 12" — making static gunlines irrelevant by advancing and still shooting at full effect. The engine is He'stan unlocking Infernus Squads to act while embarked or after unloading from Redeemers, flooding midfield with high-Strength flamer volume that punishes any opponent who clusters models or contests objectives at close range. It thrives against horde armies and multi-wound infantry blobs that can't survive the mass wound-and-burn output delivered by Aggressors and Infernus Squads pushing up together. Opponents who can deny the 12" window — through long-range high-AP shooting or fast melee threats that force the Redeemers back — leave this build without its Strength bonus and grinding against its own slow deployment.
475: Built around Assault Intercessor Squads, Crusader Squads, Scout Squads, and Intercessor Squads flooding the board in volume, anchored by Repulsor Executioners for heavy fire support and led by High Marshal Helbrecht, the Emperor's Champion, Marshals, and Castellans providing stacked command synergies. The Bastion Task Force detachment lets Battleline units Advance or Fall Back and still shoot, charge, and perform Actions, so the mass infantry never stops scoring while the Repulsor Executioners pound threats from range. This combination of skimmer firepower and sheer body count punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot clear objectives fast enough against continuous wave pressure. Where it cracks is against high-damage alpha-strike lists that can delete key infantry blocks before the detachment's mobility advantage compounds — losing tempo early against aggressive shooting unravels the scoring engine.
481: Built around multiple Knight Castellans — big, heavily armed Dominus-class walkers — this list uses the Dominus Foebreakers detachment to punish enemies hiding in terrain, gaining +1 to hit rolls against any unit sheltering in a terrain area. About two-thirds of lists add Valourstrike Lance, enabling Advancing Knights to still fire at full effectiveness via the Assault ability, turning what should be slow behemoths into mobile fire platforms. Archeotech Autoloaders appears in over three-quarters of lists, suggesting a strong emphasis on volume or sustained ranged output. The list punishes gunline armies and terrain-hugging infantry hard — anything camping in cover hands the Castellans free accuracy bonuses — but struggles against fast, low-model-count forces that can exploit activation efficiency and overwhelm the Knights' scoring footprint before the big guns find their targets.
482: Built around a Knight Castellan, Armiger Warglaives, and a Cerastus Knight Lancer, this Freeblade Company list leans on the detachment's passive durability — Feel No Pain 6+ and wound regeneration each Command phase — to keep its massive chassis on the table long enough to grind opponents out. The win condition is straightforward anti-armour pressure at range from the Castellan's heavy firepower while the Lancer and Warglaives surge forward to crack open vehicles and multi-wound targets in melee, contesting objectives with bodies that refuse to die cleanly. It punishes armour-heavy and elite lists brutally, overloading their anti-tank budget with multiple high-wound targets that self-repair between turns. Against screens, chip damage, and volume mortal wounds — tools that bypass the Feel No Pain and outpace the regeneration — the list struggles to stay relevant on secondary scoring as its slow, expensive pieces get death-by-a-thousand-cuts.
484: Built around Norn Assimilators, Biovores, Pyrovores, the Swarmlord, Norn Emissaries, and Psychophages, this list runs the Assimilation Swarm detachment to fuel a regenerating monster mash that grinds opponents down through attrition — Harvesters continuously returning wounds and slain infantry models to keep bodies on the table turn after turn. The win condition is sustained board presence: Norn Assimilators and Emissaries brawl for mid-table objectives while Biovores harass screens and Pyrovores punish infantry clusters, all while the regeneration engine makes every trade unfavorable for the opponent. It brutally punishes low-volume, high-damage shooting lists that expect to remove threats permanently, since key monsters simply refuse to die. Burst-damage alpha strike armies that can spike multiple Harvesters off the table in a single phase before regeneration triggers will crack this build open, collapsing the engine before it gets rolling.
485: Built around Norn Emissaries, Norn Assimilators, Tyrannofexes, Maleceptors, Exocrines, and the Swarmlord, this is a wall of Tyranid Monsters operating under Crusher Stampede's rule set, which rewards damaged units with bonus Hit and Wound rolls and gives full-strength Monsters boosted Objective Control. The gameplan is to plant high-OC Monsters on key objectives early, use Biovores to harass and deny backfield scoring, and let the Swarmlord flex units across the board while damaged Monsters become progressively more lethal in combat. It punishes mid-range gunlines that can wound but rarely delete Monsters cleanly, since half-dead creatures hit and wound more reliably than fresh ones. The build cracks against alpha-strike lists or high-volume anti-tank overload that can delete entire Monster units before they fall below Starting Strength and trigger those bonuses.
486: Built around near-maximum Boyz squads, Ghazghkull Thraka, multiple Warbosses, Painboys, and Bigbosses flooding the table with cheap Gretchin screens, this is a Green Tide detachment list that weaponises Sustained Hits 1 on all Boyz melee and Lethal Hits against non-Monsters and non-Vehicles on the charge. The plan is to crash wave after wave of infantry into midfield, exploit fall-back-and-charge to keep pressure permanent, and grind opponents into submission through sheer volume of melee attacks amplified by character buffs. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot absorb the attrition — a handful of Painboys keeping squads functional while Lethal Hits shreds infantry regardless of saves. High model count is also the liability: armies with mass mortal wounds, large blast weapons, or strong shooting that removes key characters before the wave lands will strip the buffs and blunt the tide before it arrives.
487: Built around Squighog Boyz, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Beastboss, Beast Snagga Boyz, Kill Rigs, and Mozrog Skragbad, backed by cheap Gretchin screens, this is a massed Beast Snagga horde that crashes into mid-table and never lets go. The engine is simple and brutal: Da Big Hunt's +1 AP against Monsters and Vehicles turns every Beast Snagga unit into an anti-armour sledgehammer, while the sheer weight of bodies floods objectives and dares opponents to trade efficiently. It punishes vehicle-heavy and monster-spam lists hardest, where the AP bonus stacks across multiple waves of Squighogs and infantry to strip saves that would otherwise hold up a conventional green tide. Anything that can screen its key pieces away with fast chaff or land a surgical alpha strike on the Beastbosses before the wave lands will crack the threat concentration and leave a horde with no teeth.
488: Built around Squighog Boyz, Ghazghkull Thraka, Mozrog Skragbad, Beastboss on Squigosaur, and Wazdakka Gutsmek as a mounted cavalry hammer, with Gretchin and Boyz in Trukks screening the advance and Lootas plus Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns providing layered fire support. The plan is to crash elite beast-riders into the midboard while cheap hordes and transports hold objectives and deny enemy scoring lanes, letting the cavalry delete priority threats and snowball board control. Horde-based armies that rely on volume attacks to neutralize elite units get punished hard, as the combination of monster cavalry and massed cheap bodies overwhelms both frontlines and flanks simultaneously. The build cracks against efficient long-range anti-armor that can strip Trukks early and disrupt the transport wave before the cavalry closes, leaving Gretchin and Boyz exposed without their delivery mechanisms.
492: Built around Custodian Guard, Allarus Custodians, Blade Champion, Custodian Wardens, Witchseekers, Vertus Praetors, and Caladius Grav-Tanks, this is a mobile, multi-threat elite infantry list running Shield Host with two-thirds of lists splashing Tharanatoi Hammerblow for Allarus deep-strike charge re-rolls. The game plan is layered threat delivery — Vertus Praetors and Caladius Grav-Tanks pressure mid-board while Allarus ingress onto priority targets and the Ka'tah selection toggles between Critical Hit fishing and AP improvement turn-by-turn to match the matchup. It punishes armies with durable but low-model-count elite infantry, where the combination of high-quality melee, mobile shooting, and flexible threat angles overwhelms targeted defenses. It cracks open against armies that can deny or punish the deep strike window, pile in anti-tank overload against the Caladius, or flood cheap bodies to screen out the charge lanes the whole engine depends on.
499: Built around Castigators, Morvenn Vahl, Paragon Warsuits, and Immolator-mounted infantry, this is a mobile armoured gunline that doubles down on Acts of Faith through Army of Faith to squeeze two faith actions per phase out of nearly every unit on the table. The win condition is layered firepower — Castigators and Exorcists suppress armour at range while Immolators push Dominion and Battle Sisters into mid-board, and Zephyrim plus jump-pack Canonesses crash flanks to clean up screens and exposed characters. It punishes static, low-mobility lists that can't contest the mid-table fast enough, letting the skimmer core maintain range control while infantry trade efficiently from transports. Where it cracks is against high-volume mortal-wound output or elite melee that can strip the Paragon Warsuits and Vahl early, collapsing the anti-armour backbone before the gunline can compensate.
505: Built around Techmarines, Redemptor, Brutalis, and Ballistus Dreadnoughts, and Repulsor Executioners, this is a mechanised armoured column that leverages the Ironstorm Spearhead's per-unit re-roll on hit, wound, or damage to squeeze maximum output from every heavy weapon salvo. The win condition is raw attrition at range — layers of Dreadnought firepower backed by Repulsor Executioners grind enemy units off the board while Techmarines keep the chassis alive and on objectives. It punishes light-vehicle and multi-wound infantry spam hard, because the volume of high-damage shots overwhelms anything that can't absorb anti-tank overload across multiple activations. It cracks open when faced with elite low-model-count lists that can alpha-strike the vehicles before Techmarines repair them, or screen-and-deny armies that starve it of targets and force it to score through a footprint it struggles to project cleanly.
517: Built around a pair of Doomsday Arks, the Silent King, Canoptek Wraiths, Technomancers, Ophydian Destroyers, and Flayed Ones, this list weaponizes the Starshatter Arsenal's core rule — adding 1 to Hit rolls against units near objectives — to turn every contested marker into a kill zone, while the Assault keyword on vehicle weapons lets Doomsday Arks threaten targets even after repositioning. The win condition is objective pressure converted directly into firepower efficiency: contest a point, shoot with boosted accuracy, clear what's sitting on it, then flood it with Wraiths or Destroyers burrowing up from beneath. It punishes slow, durable, objective-camping armies — precisely the kind that park elite infantry or vehicles on markers — because those units become the preferred targets of the hit-bonus engine. Aggressive melee threats that can bypass the objective-trigger condition and crack the Arks before they fire, or lists that contest from range without ever touching the markers, can neutralize the accuracy bonus and leave this build's damage output looking ordinary.
522: Built around Cthonian Beserks, Berehk Stornbröw, and a dense supporting cast of infantry, carriers, and armoured vehicles, this list runs Dêlve Assault Shift to drop Beserks via Deep Strike directly onto contested mid-board objectives. The plan is a relentless brawl: Kapricus Carriers and Sagitaurs (frequently with Scouts 6" from Armoured Trailblazers) deliver infantry into the thick of the fight while deep-striking Beserks threaten any exposed flank, overwhelming opponents through sheer volume and positional pressure. It punishes static gunlines that can't clear multiple threat vectors simultaneously — the combination of scouting vehicles, airborne Beserks, and a heavy vehicle anchor in the Hekaton Land Fortress creates an anti-tank and melee overload that spread-thin defences cannot handle. However, armies that deny deep strike landing zones or screen the mid-board early can neutralise the Beserk drop timing, gutting the entire offensive engine before it engages.
530: Built around Allarus Custodians, Vertus Praetors, Telemon and Contemptor-Achillus Dreadnoughts boosted by Might of the Moritoi's +2" Move and +1 to advance and charge rolls, this list layers elite close-combat threats across multiple unit types alongside Sisters of Silence screens in Witchseekers and Prosecutors. The plan is to use the dreadnoughts and Allarus as a mobile hammer — closing distance faster than opponents expect — while Shield Host's Critical Hit threshold on melee attacks (5+ unmodified) amplifies kill-chain damage output turn after turn. It punishes slow, durable infantry blobs that can't screen all vectors simultaneously, overwhelming them through layered melee threats arriving from multiple angles. It cracks apart against armies that can reliably shoot walkers off the table before they reach combat, stripping the mobility engine before it delivers.
534: Built around Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Hernkyn Pioneers, Hernkyn Yaegirs, Kapricus Carriers, Kapricus Defenders, Ûthar the Destined, Einhyr Hearthguard, a Hekaton Land Fortress, Ironkin Steeljacks with heavy volkanite disintegrators, and a Memnyr Strategist, this Farseekers list is a mid-board brawler that floods the table with transported infantry and punishing close-range firepower. 540: Built around Sanguinary Guard, jump pack Captains, Commander Dante, Sanguinary Priests, Bladeguard Veterans, Inceptors, and a Lieutenant with combi-weapon, this is a highly mobile mid-board pressure list running the Angelic Inheritors detachment, which lets you select two Angelic Legacy buffs — including Sanguinary Grace, which allows Characters to shoot and charge after Falling Back — to apply across your Character suite for the whole game. 543: Built around Drazhar, Incubi, Archons, Lady Malys, Wyches, Mandrakes, Kabalite Warriors, and a full motor pool of Venoms and Raiders, this is a classic Drukhari skimmer swarm running Kabalite Agonysts with most lists also taking Skysplinter Assault for a second detachment pick. However, elite elite-removal lists that can strip transports early expose the fragile infantry inside before they can deliver, cracking the engine before it starts.
551: Built around Rendmasters on Blood Throne, Skarbrand, Flesh Hounds, Bloodcrushers, Skullmasters, Bloodletters, and Bloodthirsters, this is a wall-to-wall Khorne Daemons assault list running the Blood Legion detachment, with the majority of lists supplementing it with Cavalcade of Chaos to let Bloodcrushers fall back and charge freely. 561: Built around Scarab Occult Terminators led by Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Rubric Marines, Sekhetar Robots, and screened by Tzaangors and Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, the Rubricae Phalanx detachment makes Rubricae models effectively immune to all damage-1 attacks, turning standard infantry weapons into wasted dice. 572: Built around Aberrants, Abominants, Purestrain Genestealers, and a Patriarch leading a massive horde of Acolytes, Neophytes, and Ridgerunners, this is Biosanctic Broodsurge charging into your face on turn one. 575: Built around Wyches, Lelith Hesperax, multiple Succubi, Hellions, and Mandrakes flooding the midfield, supported by Scourges with heavy weapons and a fast Venom/Raider skimmer layer, this is a mass-horde close-combat swarm running the Kabalite Agonysts detachment. It punishes slower elite armies that cannot clear dozens of cheap, fast bodies before getting tied up in combat, especially when Scourges threaten flanks and Cronos provides sustain. It cracks open against armies that efficiently clear hordes at range, because losing model density early collapses the board-pressure engine before the melee threats can close.
587: Built around Fulgrim, Lords Exultant, Infractors, Flawless Blades, Tormentors, and Noise Marines transported in Chaos Rhinos, this is a mobile infantry-heavy brawler running Coterie of the Conceited — a detachment that rewards you for accurately predicting how many enemy units you'll destroy each battle round, converting successful pledges into Pact points. However, lists that deny combat engagement — strong shooting gunlines, deep strike denial, or resilient bricks that refuse to die on schedule — collapse the pledge economy and leave the army scoring nothing from its defining mechanic.
588: Built around Flawless Blades, Infractors, Lord Exultants, Tormentors, Lucius the Eternal, and Fulgrim, this is a transport-heavy melee swarm that delivers infantry into charge range through Rhinos before unleashing the Peerless Bladesmen detachment's charge bonus — choosing Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1 on every fighting unit that charged. The win condition is turn-two contact: screen-clear with Fights First Flawless Blades via Spectacle of Slaughter, then flood mid-table with multiple lethal combat units simultaneously so the opponent cannot trade efficiently. It punishes low-model-count elite melee armies that lack screening depth, overwhelming them through volume of attacks amplified by the charge abilities. Armies with strong shooting that can strip transports before they deliver their cargo, or that castle back to deny charge lanes entirely, crack this list open before it generates its signature threat.
589: Built around winged Daemon Princes, Lords Exultant, Infractors, Tormentors, Noise Marines, and Flawless Blades riding Chaos Rhinos forward, with Defilers and Lucius the Eternal rounding out the core, this is an aggressive mechanised brawler operating under the Coterie of the Conceited detachment, pledging kill counts to Slaanesh each round to generate Pact points. The win condition is a rolling mid-table pressure game: deliver Infractors and Tormentors via Rhinos into close range, stack kills to meet pledges, and convert Pact economy into compounding offensive output across multiple turns. It punishes slower, infantry-dense gunlines that can't strip Rhinos fast enough before the cargo unloads, and the mobile anti-armour profile means armoured lists can't simply turtle. Lists that can eliminate the transport layer before disembarkation — fast, high-volume anti-tank that collapses multiple Rhinos in one shooting phase — shatter the kill-pledge math and leave expensive melee units stranded short of targets.
592: Built around Purifier Squads, Castellan Crowe, Grand Master Nemesis Dreadknights, Strike Squads, and Brotherhood Terminators, this list uses the Warpbane Task Force detachment to project Hallowed Ground across the battlefield — anchored in your own deployment zone and extending wherever Purifiers stand. The win condition is controlling No Man's Land objectives to expand Hallowed Ground mid-game while Dreadknights and Terminators hammer forward, creating a self-reinforcing positional engine that scores through area denial as much as raw kills. It punishes static, low-mobility lists that can't contest mid-board early, as the Purifier-Crowe anchor makes the deployment zone almost untouchable while Dreadknights threaten anything that lingers. Highly mobile, elite-killing armies that can contest multiple Purifier bubbles simultaneously and deny the No Man's Land threshold will fracture the Hallowed Ground engine before it fully activates.
594: Built around Armiger Warglaives, Armiger Helverins, and a Knight Paladin under Freeblade Company, this list fields a swarm of mid-sized Knights that each regenerate a wound per Command phase and carry a blanket Feel No Pain 6+, making the whole force grindier than its individual toughness suggests. The plan is to drown opponents in sustained mobile anti-armour output — Helverins punishing at range while Warglaives close and threaten every angle — with the Paladin providing a heavyweight anchor that holds or contests central objectives. It punishes armies reliant on moderate-damage multi-wound attacks, since the drip-feed healing and FNP collectively outpace anything that can't delete a Knight outright. However, lists capable of concentrated alpha-strike damage — overloading a single Knight before healing matters — or those that stack enough mortal-wound output to bypass the FNP entirely will crack the durability engine before it can regenerate its way back into contention.
599: Built around multiple squads of Neurolictor, Lictor, Genestealer, Broodlord, Von Ryan's Leapers, Hyperadapted Raveners, and Raveners alongside Biovores, Neurotyrant, Zoanthropes, Hormagaunts, and Deathleaper, this is a deep-striking swarm using the Ambush Predators detachment to flood the board with hidden threats that materialize where the opponent least wants them. The win condition is threat saturation — so many independently dangerous deep-strike and fast-moving units arrive simultaneously that the opponent cannot cover every angle, letting Genestealers and Broodlords tear through infantry while Lictor and Neurolictor hunt exposed Characters with re-rolled hit rolls. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count elite lists that cannot screen enough table space to prevent multiple high-value contact threats landing simultaneously. It cracks open against heavy melee boards or dense screens that absorb the assault waves before they bite, and against armies with enough board presence to deny the landing zones that the whole engine depends on.
602: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka leading waves of Boyz and Gretchin, supported by Painboys, Warbosses, Wazdakka Gutsmek, Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Flash Gitz, Lootas, Tankbustas, and Zodgrod Wortsnagga under the Freebooter Krew detachment, this is a mass-horde army that layers melee brutality with serious mid-range firepower. The plan is to flood objectives with bodies while Ghazghkull's mob crashes into the midboard, Painboys keep key units fighting longer, and the gunline elements bleed opponents at range before the brawl begins. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't absorb the sheer volume of wounds and activations across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. It cracks open against high-mobility forces that can isolate and eliminate the gunline elements before the horde closes distance, or anything with enough precision firepower to remove Ghazghkull early.
603: Built around Wazdakka Gutsmek, Ghazghkull Thraka, Flash Gitz, Lootas, Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns and Dakkariggs, Tankbustas, and massed Gretchin and Boyz riding Trukks under the Freebooter Krew and More Dakka detachments, this is a mid-board brawling gunline that floods the table with bodies and layered shooting. It punishes static elite armies that can't handle simultaneous anti-tank and anti-infantry overload across multiple threat vectors. It cracks open against fast alpha-strike lists that can isolate and pop Trukks before delivery, stranding key units in the open.
605: Built around Meganobz, Nobz, Ghazghkull Thraka, Warboss, and Warboss in Mega Armour delivered inside Trukks, with Gretchin flooding objectives, this is Bully Boyz — a mid-board brawler that gives every Meganobz and Nobz melee attack Sustained Hits 1, stacking hit volume to lethal levels. The plan is to surge transports into the midfield early, disembark elite melee units into the opponent's face, and grind through layered combat phases while Gretchin screen-and-deny on primary objectives. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't absorb repeated waves of Sustained Hits 1 melee output across multiple squads hitting simultaneously. It cracks against mass shooting gunlines that can delete Trukks before the cargo deploys, stranding expensive melee units in the open with no reach.
611: Built around Khorne Berzerkers, Jakhals, Eightbound, Exalted Eightbound, Slaughterbound, Angron, Khârn the Betrayer, and Chaos Rhinos ferrying troops into contact, this is a wall-to-wall melee horde that lives entirely inside the Berzerker Warband's charge buff — every unit that charges gains +1 Attack and +2 Strength on all melee weapons, turning even chaff into a credible threat. 612: Built around Exalted Eightbound, Eightbound, Slaughterbound, Jakhals, Daemon Prince of Khorne, and Goremongers under the Possessed Slaughterband detachment, this army is a wave of Possessed infantry that surges forward and brawls for mid-table control. It cracks under high-volume, high-AP shooting that deletes whole squads before Brazen Fury triggers, or against lists that deny mid-board engagement through screens and superior threat projection.

618: Built around Hekaton Land Fortresses, Sagitaurs, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and a deep roster of Hearthkyn, Pioneers, Hearthguard, Yaegirs, Beserks, and Ironkin Steeljacks, this is a mechanised mid-table brawler that uses Scouts 6" on Sagitaurs to pre-position its transport infantry aggressively from turn one. 619: Built around double Hekaton Land Fortresses supported by Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Einhyr Hearthguard, Ironkin Steeljacks with heavy volkanite disintegrators, and a full complement of Hernkyn scouts and Kapricus Carriers, this list plays a grinding mid-board gunline backed by durable armour. 620: Built around Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Sagitaurs with Scouts 6", and massed infantry riding Kapricus Carriers, this Armoured Trailblazers list floods the midboard with bodies and heavy firepower from turn one. 621: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Hernkyn Pioneers, Sagitaurs, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and a Hekaton Land Fortress core, this is a mid-board brawler that floods the table with durable infantry delivered by Kapricus Carriers and Sagitaurs while Hernkyn Yaegirs and Hearthkyn Warriors contest secondaries. 626: Built around Defilers, Poxwalkers, Malignant Plaguecasters, Typhus, Mortarion, Noxious Blightbringers, and Myphitic Blight-Haulers under the Paragons of Putrescence detachment, this list weaponizes extended Contagion Range — Death Guard Characters pushing that aura out to 12" — to layer lethal attrition across the entire midfield. 627: Built around Deathshroud Terminators, Lords of Contagion, Malignant Plaguecasters, Typhus, and Rotigus, all operating under Paragons of Putrescence to push Contagion Range out to 12" on characters and blanket the board in overlapping plague auras, with Poxwalkers flooding objectives as disposable, self-replenishing chaff. It punishes medium-toughness infantry lists brutally, as the combination of wide Contagion coverage and Deathshroud melee overloads saves and shreds blobs before they can trade efficiently. However, fast elite armies that can isolate the Terminators before their auras activate, or high-volume mortal-wound output that bypasses the Death Guard's own resilience, can crack the engine open before the attrition engine gets running.
629: Built around Deathshroud Terminators, Lords of Contagion, Plague Marines, Poxwalkers, Lords of Virulence, Foetid Bloat-Drones, Malignant Plaguecasters, and Plagueburst Crawlers, this list layers both Mortarion's Hammer and Paragons of Putrescence to stack Afflicted status onto enemy units at range while extended Contagion from Death Guard Characters saturates the midboard. 634: Built around Atalan Jackals, Achilles Ridgerunners, Goliath Rockgrinders, Acolyte Hybrids with hand flamers, Reductus Saboteurs, and Purestrain Genestealers, this is a high-volume Genestealer Cult swarm running Outlander Claw to hold objectives with mounted and vehicle units that are nearly impossible to dislodge. 641: Built around Deathwing Knights, Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Inner Circle Companions, Ravenwing Black Knights, Sammael, Outrider Squads, Scouts, and Ravenwing Command Squad under Company of Hunters, this list blends elite terminator hammers with a fast-moving biker cavalry arm that shoots freely after falling back or advancing. 642: Built around Deathwing Knights, Chaplains in Terminator Armour, Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Inner Circle Companions, Scouts, and Outriders, this Interrogation Conclave list uses elite melee terminators and characters as its hammer while fast-moving biker screens and scout units provide flexible board presence. 643: Built around Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Sanguinary Guard, Lemartes, Sanguinary Priests, Captain with Jump Pack, Commander Dante, and Bladeguard Veterans, this is a Liberator Assault Group list that floods the board with charging infantry, converting every successful charge into +2 Strength and +1 Attack across all melee weapons. It punishes slower, fragile midfield armies that cannot screen effectively against multi-vector jump infantry delivery. 648: Built around Defilers, Warp Talons, Raptors, Chosen, a Jump Pack Chaos Lord, Cultist Mobs, Red Corsairs Raiders, Huron Blackheart, and Masters of the Maelstrom, this Murdertalon Raiders list is a flying-infantry brawler that pairs heavy walker firepower with aggressive deep-strike pressure. 656: Built around the Avatar of Khaine, Fuegan, Lhykhis, Warp Spiders, Fire Dragons, Howling Banshees, Striking Scorpions, Swooping Hawks, Rangers, War Walkers, and Corsair Voidreavers, supported by Eldrad Ulthran — this is a full-spectrum Aspect Warrior roster with no single detachment lock, splitting roughly evenly across Warhost, Armoured Warhost, and Seer Council. 658: Built around three C'tan Shards — Void Dragon, Nightbringer, and Deceiver — alongside Ophydian Destroyers and Imotekh the Stormlord, this list runs the Pantheon of Woe detachment to stack Distortion Fields auras across multiple Monster-keyword gods, shredding armour saves on everything nearby.
