666: Built around waves of Daemonettes, Fiends, Keepers of Secrets, the Contorted Epitome, the Tormentbringer, and the Masque of Slaanesh, this is a hyper-mobile Slaanesh horde that weaponises both Legion of Excess and Warptide: Daemonettes advance, shoot, and charge in the same activation, while the entire army can fall back and charge again to never cede combat. The win condition is perpetual melee presence — swamping objectives with expendable Daemonette screens, cycling Fiends and Keepers into kill targets turn after turn, and grinding opponents out of scoring positions through sheer attrition across multiple combat phases. It punishes slow or fragile elite lists that cannot disengage from combat, because the fall-back-and-charge loop denies the standard escape valve and lets this army dictate every fight on its own terms. It cracks against high-volume mortal-wound output or strong shooting armies that can delete Daemonette screens before the advance-and-charge engine gets rolling, leaving the pricier combat pieces dangerously exposed.
668: Built around multiple Lords of Change and Kairos Fateweaver commanding packs of Screamers, Flamers, and Pink Horrors, this Scintillating Legion list plays pure Tzeentch daemon mobility and volume — fast, flickering, and hard to pin down. The engine is Warptide-fuelled Screamers advancing and still charging into mid-board objectives while Flamers pour mortal-wound-style layered lethality into infantry screens, and Flux tokens bail out critical rolls at every stage of the kill chain. It punishes static gunlines and low-model elite armies that can't handle simultaneous threats arriving from multiple vectors across the whole board. It cracks under pressure when faced with durable, high-volume shooting that strips units before Flux tokens can compensate, or massed anti-horde saturation that overwhelms its relatively fragile daemon bodies.
672: Built around Defilers, Infractors in Chaos Rhinos, Lords Exultant, Tormentors, Flawless Blades, Maulerfiends, and Lucius the Eternal under the Court of the Phoenician, this is a mobile mid-table brawler that floods the board with transported infantry and daemon engines. The win condition is using Rhino-delivered Infractors and Tormentors to contest and hold primaries while Lords Exultant amplify nearby units, with Maulerfiends and Defilers applying mobile anti-armour pressure that forces opponents to split resources. It punishes slower gunlines and elite infantry-heavy lists that cannot handle simultaneous threats from multiple daemon engines and disembarking assault infantry. Armies that can screen efficiently or project ranged anti-tank overload early will strip the daemon engine core before the charge-fuelled Sensational Performance payoff comes online.
680: Built around Caanok Var, Terminator Assault Squads, an Ancient in Terminator Armour, Librarians in Terminator Armour, Ballistus Dreadnoughts, and Scout screens, this Hammer of Avernii list chains Caanok Var's RECALCULATING ability to keep a fresh Oath of Moment target locked in every round, feeding persistent re-roll-wound-1s to a heavily armoured Terminator core that grinds forward with Banner support keeping squads fighting. The win condition is sustained kill pressure — using Var to redirect Oath onto the next priority threat the moment one dies, ensuring the melee hammer and Ballistus gunfire are always hitting at full efficiency rather than bleeding output mid-battle. It punishes elite-infantry and vehicle-heavy lists that present distinct, sequenced targets, because the Oath chain means killing one unit actively empowers the attack on the next. Lists that spam chaff or split across many small units can dilute the Oath focus and tie down the Terminator bricks before Var can redirect, stalling the kill engine.
681: Built around Terminator Squads, Librarians in Terminator Armour, Centurion Devastator Squads, Scouts, Intercessors, Inceptors, Incursors, Terminator Assault Squads, and Aethon Shaan under the Librarius Conclave detachment, this is a ranged-weight Space Marines list that layers psychic discipline selection across its psykers to tune output round by round. The win condition is sustained volume fire from Centurion Devastators and Inceptors, with Divination Discipline re-rolls sharpening the kill chain against hard targets while Scouts and Incursors flood forward to hold primaries and screen out deep strikers. Temporal Corridor on a Librarian in Terminator Armour enables late-game repositioning of elite infantry, letting the list threaten objectives it appeared locked out of. Lists running the Shadowmark Talon secondary detachment gain ranged durability against anything outside 12", but the build struggles badly against fast melee threats that can close that gap and strip its fragile backfield screens before the gunline can respond.
683: Built around stacked Intercessor squads, Librarians, and Heavy Intercessors, this is a dense, slow-moving gunline that exploits the Bastion Task Force's core rule to Advance onto objectives while still shooting and performing Actions with its Battleline units — removing the usual trade-off between movement and firepower. The win condition is objective saturation: flood mid-table with cheap, mobile-without-penalty Battleline bodies, score primaries through Actions they complete while advancing, then erode enemy units through volume of fire and the post-attack suppression effect on anything they hit. It punishes horde and mid-tier infantry armies badly, stacking Librarian psychic disciplines — Divination's re-rolls or Pyromancy's burn output — to make massed bolter fire surprisingly lethal. Concentrated elite melee threats or hard anti-infantry overload can crack it open, because the units are individually fragile and the list struggles to project meaningful threat across the entire board simultaneously.
687: Built around War Dog Executioners, Karnivores, Brigands, and Stalkers swarming forward under Helhunt Lance's aura-sharing mechanic — which feeds Titanic units like the Knight Ruinator and Knight Abominant into their own pack buffs — with Nurglings providing cheap screening mass. The win condition is layered anti-armour attrition: War Dogs independently threaten vehicles and monsters from multiple angles simultaneously, while the Titanic anchor pieces exploit the aura feedback loop to punch even harder into high-value targets. This build punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot deal with anti-armour overload across six-plus activations, forcing opponents to prioritize targets they simply cannot cover. However, a fast infantry-heavy list that floods the board can screen out the detection-range pressure from Hunting Warpack and deny the War Dogs clean charges, exploiting the limited body count to contest objectives before the Knights can clear them.
689: Built around Grand Master Nemesis Dreadknights, Purgation Squads, Purifier Squads, Strike Squads, and Castellan Crowe, this Brotherhood Strike list floods the table with mobile infantry delivered via transports and punishes landings with deep-strike re-rolls on hits and wounds. The core engine is Purgation Squads pinning enemy units and forcing battle-shock rolls at -1 through Fires of Purgation, degrading opponent efficiency while Dreadknights and Crowe clean up weakened targets. It excels against horde armies and infantry-dense lists where skimmer fire and layered lethality compound across multiple units simultaneously. It struggles against elite, durable armies that shrug off battle-shock and can absorb the deep-strike shooting burst before counter-punching through its relatively fragile infantry backbone.
695: Built around Logan Grimnar, multiple squads of Wolf Guard Terminators, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Arjac Rockfist, Wolf Guard Headtakers, and Intercessors, this Saga of the Great Wolf list is a mid-table brawling machine that selects a rotating Hunting Pack each Command phase — cycling between charge re-rolls and other buffs — to amplify whichever unit group is about to hit the enemy hardest. The win condition is crashing Terminator-heavy combat squads into the midfield while Logan provides command presence and Bjorn anchors an immovable firebase, grinding opponents off objectives through attrition and melee superiority rather than speed or shooting alone. It punishes lists that rely on fragile elite infantry or light vehicles, overwhelming them with durable, heavily armoured bodies that are difficult to shift and lethal in close quarters. It struggles against armies that can outrange it consistently or use deep strike and screening to deny the charge, since its mobile toolkit depends on actually reaching the fight in good order.
700: Built around the Cerastus Knight Lancer, Canis Rex, Armiger Warglaives, and Knight Errants operating under the Freeblade Company detachment, this list fields a mobile, self-sustaining battlegroup where every model carries Feel No Pain 6+ and ticks back a wound each Command phase, making the army frustratingly hard to fully kill. The win condition is sustained melee and mid-range pressure — Lancers crash into priority targets while Warglaives clean flanks, and the incremental wound recovery keeps models on the table long enough to score secondaries that slower armies can't deny. It punishes vehicle-heavy lists through anti-armour overload across multiple threat vectors simultaneously, forcing opponents to split fire or cede board control to hard-to-remove Knights. Its weakness is concentrated high-volume anti-tank or mortal wound output that can spike a big Knight off the table before regeneration matters, cracking the army's point-efficiency model in a single turn.
708: Built around Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, Allarus Custodians, the Blade Champion, Trajann Valoris, a Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator Armour, Prosecutors, Witchseekers, and Vertus Praetors under Lions of the Emperor, this is a wall of elite infantry that gets +1 to hit and wound whenever a unit fights in isolation — so the entire army is engineered to spread out and duel independently rather than cluster. The win condition is controlled board domination: isolate each unit six inches from its nearest friend, trigger the detachment bonus, then grind opponents off objectives through layered lethality across multiple simultaneous combats. It punishes mid-density armies that lack the volume to trade evenly against elite, self-sufficient fighting units, and the mobile toolkit of jetbikes and deep-striking Allarus gives it genuine flexibility to dictate where those isolated engagements happen. Horde spam or mass-screening armies that can consistently park cheap bodies within six inches of your units will suppress the Lions bonus and blunt the entire damage output of the list.
717: Built around Morvenn Vahl, Castigators, Paragon Warsuits, Immolators, and a deep infantry core of Dominion Squads, Celestian Sacresants, Celestian Insidiants, and a Hospitaller, this is a mobile armoured firing line that deliberately accepts attrition to get stronger — the Hallowed Martyrs detachment adds +1 to Hit when a unit is below Starting Strength and +1 to Wound when Below Half-strength, meaning every casualty your opponent inflicts tightens the noose. The plan is to push Immolator-borne infantry onto objectives while Castigators and Vahl hammer armour, then use Saintly Example to spread that wound-bonus across the line as units bleed, snowballing combat efficiency mid-game. It punishes aggressive armies that trade into it freely, since every kill activates or deepens the damage bonus, turning a normal war of attrition into a losing proposition for the attacker. Extreme alpha-strike lists that can erase whole units in a single activation — bypassing the below-half trigger entirely — or armies with enough mortal output to delete squads before they fire back are the sharpest counters.
718: Built around Immolators, Castigators, Dominion Squads, Paragon Warsuits, Morvenn Vahl, and Seraphim, this is a mobile fire-platform army running the Bringers of Flame detachment — every Adepta Sororitas ranged weapon gains Assault, and attacks within 6" gain +1 Strength, turning constant advance into a damage amplifier rather than a penalty. The plan is to close distance aggressively, parking Immolators and Dominions at point-blank range to spike Strength on melta and flamer weapons while Castigators pressure armour from mid-board and Vahl anchors the kill line. It punishes low-toughness elite armies and light vehicle spam by volume-overloading with souped-up short-range firepower from units that can move-and-shoot without penalty. Armies that can deny the 6" sweet spot through long-range alpha strikes or deep-board screening leave this list shooting at half efficiency with no fallback threat range.
719: Built around the Triumph of Saint Katherine, Repentia Squads, Arco-Flagellants, Celestian Sacresants, and Intranzia Fraye, this Penitent Host list is a mass-horde melee engine that uses Rhinos to deliver waves of cheap, violent infantry directly into the opponent's face. The Triumph's aura keeps Repentias and Arco-Flagellants fed back into the fight through wound recovery, while Ministorum Priests and the Hospitaller layer on buffs and healing to sustain the grind; the Penitent Host's rotating Vows of Atonement juice movement and fight efficiency exactly when each wave needs it. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't generate enough kill volume to outpace the resurrection loop before the melee units reach them inside Rhinos. Armies with strong skew shooting or fight-on-death mechanics can surgically kill the Triumph early, collapsing the sustainability engine and leaving the horde without its crucial attrition advantage.
720: Built around Morvenn Vahl, Celestian Sacresants, Paragon Warsuits, and Hospitallers backed by Castigators, Immolators, and a deep command bench of Canonesses and Junith Eruita, this list floods the board with durable, self-healing infantry packed into transports and supported by ranged fire from skimmer platforms. The plan is to pressure multiple objectives simultaneously — Hospitallers keep squads above replacement thresholds while Morvenn and the Sacresants punch through elite targets in melee, and the Castigators and Immolators strip screens at range. It punishes mid-density infantry armies that cannot sustain a war of attrition against constant healing and layered lethal output across all phases. However, lists that concentrate extreme damage into a single alpha strike can outpace the healing engine before it stabilises, and the build's spread across four different detachments signals it hasn't settled on a single coherent identity, leaving it tactically inconsistent at the top tables.
725: Built around Sammael, Lion El'Jonson, Azrael, Ravenwing Command Squads, Outrider Squads, Land Speeder Vengances, and a swarm of Land Speeders and Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, this is a hyper-mobile Dark Angels force running Company of Hunters to fire on the move and fall back into shooting without penalty, with most lists adding Darkflight Pursuit to strip cover from Ravenwing flyers. The engine is advance-and-shoot harassment at scale — skimmer and bike units flood mid-table turn one, contest objectives under pressure, and layer anti-armour output from Thunderstrikes and Vengances while character support from Lion and Azrael keeps key units sticky and lethal. It punishes static gunlines and slow melee armies that can't stop an aggressive advance, drowning them in mobile anti-tank before they can set up meaningful return fire. It cracks under concentrated high-AP shooting or fast melee threats that can catch and delete individual speeders before the army's distributed damage trades efficiently.
726: Built around Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Deathwing Knights, and Inner Circle Companions, this list fields an elite wall of Adeptus Astartes Infantry and Mounted units shielded by the detachment's core rule: any attack with Strength exceeding the target's Toughness suffers -1 to its Wound roll, making the whole force significantly harder to damage than it looks on paper. The plan is to push heavily armoured melee threats up the middle behind scout screens while Azrael and the Lion provide command support, grinding objectives through sheer durability rather than speed. It punishes lists that rely on mid-Strength, high-volume shooting to crack tough targets, since that wound-roll penalty shuts down the most efficient damage brackets. Dedicated high-AP, low-volume anti-tank or flat-damage weaponry that bypasses wound rolls entirely cracks this build open, as does anything that simply out-ranges and kites the relatively slow infantry core.
727: Built around Chaos Terminators, Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Mutilators, Cultist Mobs, Kravek Morne, and Red Corsairs Raiders, the Cabal of Chaos is a mid-table brawler that floods the board with bodies and hard-hitting elite infantry. The engine runs through Dark Pacts: Psyker units gain +1 Strength on ranged attacks when they pact, turning Sorcerer-led Terminator blobs into overcharged kill threats while Mutilators and Kravek close the distance under cultist screens. It punishes gunlines and low-model elite armies that struggle to clear volume, as multiple Terminator and Mutilator squads absorb fire while cultists and Raiders contest secondaries. Armies capable of sustained high-volume AP output can crack it open by stripping the cultist screens early and isolating the expensive elite units before the pact buffs come online.
728: Built around Chaos Terminator Squads, Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Mutilators, Obliterators, Warp Talons, Raptors, a Chaos Lord with Jump Pack, Kravek Morne, and Cultist Mobs, this list layers two detachments: Murdertalon Raiders' hit-roll bonuses against weakened or battle-shocked enemies, and Warpstrike Champions' end-of-turn redeployment of Terminators, Obliterators, and Mutilators to keep pressure fresh. The win condition is attrition through repositioning — teleporting heavy-hitting units off objectives mid-fight to redeploy where the opponent is already bleeding, then cashing in the Murdertalon re-rolls against half-strength targets to snowball kills. It punishes slower midfield armies that can't rapidly kill entire units, since chipping units into half-strength triggers compounding hit bonuses while the teleport engine denies clean answers. However, lists that can alpha-strike multiple units simultaneously collapse the snowball before it starts, and with no persistent -1 to-hit outside reactive conditions, focused elite shooting tears through Terminators before the attrition loop activates.
738: Built around Technomancers, Plasmancers, and Illuminor Szeras flanked by Canoptek Wraiths, Ophydian Destroyers, Tomb Blades, Scarab Swarms, and Immortals, this Cryptek Conclave army is a shape-shifting mobile toolkit that dynamically assigns Anti-Infantry, Anti-Mounted, Ignores Cover, or Heavy to its Cryptek shooting every phase. The engine is overwhelming flexibility — Tomb Blades deep strike into position for +1 to hit on ingress, Ophydian Destroyers and Wraiths pressure mid-board, and Immortals with Hand of the Dynasty's Assault rule advance and shoot without sacrificing actions, all while the Void Dragon provides a hard anti-vehicle beatstick. It punishes opponents who commit to a single defensive posture, since switching weapon profiles mid-game dismantles one-trick screens and armor stacks alike. It struggles against lists that force unfavorable early trades, as its moderate durability means attrition over several turns exposes the Crypteks before they can cycle through enough profile-switching to dominate.
739: Built around Skorpekh Lords leading Skorpekh Destroyers and Ophydian Destroyers, Canoptek Wraiths screening C'tan shards of the Void Dragon and Nightbringer, and supported by Technomancers, Canoptek Reanimators, Illuminor Szeras, Nekrosor Ammentar, and Imotekh the Stormlord, this Awakened Dynasty force runs a deep roster of elite threats that hit harder across the board — every model in a CHARACTER-led unit adds 1 to its Hit rolls. The win condition is multi-vector pressure: C'tan shards threaten high-value targets while Skorpekh units deep strike or surge through screens to dismantle midfield brawlers, with Reanimators and Technomancers recycling wounds to maintain board presence and score attrition-based secondaries. It punishes elite-light armies that cannot answer simultaneous threats from multiple angles, overloading damage-prevention tools through sheer volume of dangerous units. It cracks under concentrated alpha-strike pressure targeting the support characters before Reanimator loops come online, and struggles against armies with enough cheap bodies to screen out the melee threats entirely.
754:
Built around Grand Master in Nemesis Dreadknights, vanilla Nemesis Dreadknights, Interceptor Squads, Strike Squads, Purifier Squads, Purgation Squads, Brotherhood Terminators, and Castellan Crowe, this is a mobile psychic melee hammer that layers multiple detachment tricks across a toolbox roster with no single defining detachment — roughly half the field runs Banishers for the Leadership-gated Sustained Hits or Lethal Hits on melee, while Immaterial Interdiction turns Interceptors into post-shoot surge threats.

The win condition is threat saturation: the Grand Masters and Dreadknights teleport into engagement range while Purgation Squads pin and battle-shock targets, and Interceptors surge to contest or cut off retreat, creating overlapping pressure that forces opponents to react to multiple closing hammers simultaneously.

It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot screen every angle, since multiple deep-striking hulks arriving with melee reach and Banishers-fuelled Sustained Hits can delete key pieces before a response is possible.

However, the list struggles against high-volume shooting that can strip Dreadknights before they engage, and its below-50% win rate reflects genuine fragility against armies that can alpha its slow walkers or bury it in more objectives than its infantry base can reliably hold.
761: Built around the Knight Crusader's heavy firepower, the Cerastus Knight Atrapos's precision anti-armour output, and Armiger Warglaives providing aggressive forward pressure, this Freeblade Company list leans into Feel No Pain 6+ and per-turn wound regeneration to keep its big bodies on the table longer than opponents expect. The win condition is sustained ranged attrition — the Crusader saturates midfield with volume fire while the Atrapos hunts high-value armoured targets, and the Warglaives threaten flanks to force priority decisions across multiple vectors. This build punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to kill through layered durability, particularly those relying on alpha-strike damage to neutralise Knights before they can shoot. It cracks open against high-volume mortal wound output or armies that can concentrate enough anti-tank to overwhelm wound regeneration before objectives are secured.
767: Built around wave after wave of Boyz backed by Ghazghkull Thraka, multiple Painboys, Warbosses, Wazdakka Gutsmek, Zodgrod Wortsnagga, Gretchin screens, Kommandos, and Flash Gitz — running Equatorial Hordes and Freebooter Krew — this is an overwhelming green tide that layers melee muscle with ranged punch and surgical infiltration. The plan is to flood every midboard zone with bodies, use Gretchin to screen and deny counterplay while Boyz and characters grind opponents off objectives through sheer attrition and stacked durability from Painboys. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot match the kill-per-point economy needed to clear continuous waves of orky infantry before the melee brawl engulfs them. Armies with wide-area high-volume shooting or mortal-wound output can degrade the horde faster than the Painboy sustain can compensate, cracking the engine before it closes distance.
787: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Captains with Jump Packs, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Lemartes, Sanguinary Priests, Bladeguard Veterans, Commander Dante, and Mephiston, with Scout squads providing board presence, this is a highly mobile infantry swarm running Legacy of Grace and, in most lists, Stormlance Task Force to enable advance-and-charge across the entire force. The plan is to flood mid-table with buffed jump infantry, leveraging the +1 to advance and charge rolls to consistently close distance and overwhelm objectives through melee volume while Priests and support characters keep the assault elements alive and cycling. It punishes slower elite armies that lack the screen depth to absorb multiple simultaneous charge threats, since the list can engage from multiple angles in the same turn. However, it cracks against armies with robust shooting at range — stripped of its infantry before the charge lands, the list has no durable backline to fall back on.
809: Built around Eldrad Ulthran, multiple Warlock Conclaves, Rangers, Storm Guardians, Fuegan with Fire Dragons, War Walkers, Farseers, Howling Banshees, Farseer Skyrunners, and an Avatar of Khaine, this list runs Path of the Outcast alongside Seer Council to combine a Fate dice pool with layered Ranger-based screening. The engine is a wave of overlapping lethal-zone bubbles — Rangers expose hidden enemies through their detection-range spike while Fuegan and Fire Dragons deliver concentrated anti-armour delete, War Walkers pour mobile firepower into softened targets, and the Seer Council Fate dice let key Stratagems fire on demand. It punishes elite low-model-count lists badly, flooding the board with cheap Storm Guardian screens and Warlock buffs that make every removal trade inefficient. Armies that can alpha-strike the psychic support characters or overload the screening layers with high-volume mortal wounds crack the structure before the Fate engine gets rolling.
810: Built around Troupes, Starweavers, Troupe Masters, Falcons, Skyweavers, Rangers, and Solitaires, this is a Harlequins-heavy skimmer swarm running Serpent's Brood and Armoured Warhost together — every disembarking Troupe triggers Sustained Hits 1 on its weapons while Aeldari vehicles fire on the move with Assault. The plan is to surge Starweavers forward, disembark Troupes into melee with Sustained Hits 1 stacked on top of Troupe Master buffs, and bury opponents in layered lethal-hit attacks before they can stabilise. This punishes static, low-mobility armies that cannot prevent the transport-drop threat chain from reaching their key pieces turn one or two. However, the paper-thin durability of Harlequins infantry means anything that can shut down the transports early — or force disembarkation out of threat range — collapses the entire delivery system.
812: Built around Windriders, War Walkers, Farseer Skyrunners, Warlock Skyrunners, and Shroud Runners, this is a fast-moving vehicle and mounted force running Armoured Warhost alongside Windrider Host, letting the entire skimmer core shoot after advancing and deploy mounted units from Strategic Reserves a round early. The win condition is layered mobile firepower — Windriders and War Walkers pour out [ASSAULT]-boosted ranged attacks while psyker support from the Farseer and Warlocks amplifies the kill chain, scoring through eliminating threats and contesting with fast bodies. It punishes infantry-heavy and lightly armoured lists that can't handle volume fire from units that advance-and-shoot with full effectiveness across multiple threat vectors. However, it struggles against durable elite armies with hard anti-vehicle overload, as the chassis are individually fragile and losing key mounted pieces early collapses the tempo engine entirely.
818: Built around Tech-Priest Enginseers and Cadian Shock Troops as the backbone, this Steel Hammer list fields a rotating cast of super-heavy vehicles — Doomhammers, Stormswords, Baneblades, and Baneswords — supported by Hellhounds and Scout Sentinels for screening and harassment. The win condition is pure attrition through massed Titanic firepower: Steel Hammer lets these super-heavies shoot into and through engaged units, meaning opponents can't easily tarpit them, while Enginseers keep the machines operational and the infantry screen holds objectives. It punishes heavy-armour lists and densely packed formations that can't close the distance fast enough to avoid repeated bombardment from multiple super-heavy platforms. However, aggressive alpha-strike armies or elite melee forces that can rapidly reach engagement range and tie up multiple vehicles simultaneously will bleed it dry before the gunline can reposition.
827: Built around Terminator Assault Squads, Bladeguard Veterans, Librarians (including Librarian in Terminator Armour), Marneus Calgar, and Scout and Intercessor screening bodies, this list runs the Librarius Conclave detachment to cycle psychic disciplines each battle round — Divination for re-rolls when trading into hard targets, Biomancy to push melee threats up the board faster, and Pyromancy as a situational punish tool. The win condition is controlling objectives with durable melee infantry buffed by the round-by-round discipline selection, layering Reclamation Force's AP improvement on objective-range melee attacks and its defensive resilience on held markers to grind out Primary while the Terminators and Bladeguard punish anything that contests. It punishes medium-armour melee armies that want to trade into objectives, where the AP buff and discipline flexibility make every fight phase efficient. It cracks against hard ranged gunlines that can clear screens early and pick off the slow Terminator core before it closes, since the build lacks the raw shooting output to threaten at distance.
837: Built around nearly two Repulsor Executioners per list, a deep bench of Marshals and Castellans, the Emperor's Champion, and Scout and Assault Intercessor screens, this is a Gladius Task Force gunline that layers heavy armour over a mass of cheap infantry. The core engine is the Devastator Doctrine's advance-and-shoot rule on the Repulsor Executioners, letting the tanks reposition aggressively while maintaining full firepower output, with Marshals and Castellans buffing both the armour and the foot soldiers pushing objectives underneath. It punishes infantry-heavy and mid-range shooting armies that cannot efficiently answer multiple T12+ vehicles while simultaneously contesting every objective with a wall of bodies. Dedicated high-volume anti-tank or multi-damage weapons that can crack two heavy tanks early crack this list open, because once the Executioners die the scoring infantry lack the teeth to threaten back.
842: Built around Raveners, Hyperadapted Raveners, Trygon, The Red Terror, and a dense supporting cast of Biovores, Zoanthropes, Hormagaunts, Von Ryan's Leapers, Neurotyrant, Neurolictor, Maleceptor, The Swarmlord, and Lictor, this Subterranean Assault list weaponizes the Burrower keyword to flood the midboard from underground on turn two, trading traditional deployment pressure for a coordinated eruption threat. The engine is volume and coordination: Raveners and Hyperadapted Raveners punch into mid-table objectives while Biovore chip damage and Zoanthrope psychic weight strip screens, forcing opponents to either overcommit defensively or cede scoring real estate. It punishes static elite gunlines that lack the bodies to hold multiple zones simultaneously, overwhelming their footprint with a multi-angle midfield brawl that static positioning cannot answer. Against fast aggressive armies that contest the board early or heavy anti-infantry saturation that bleeds the swarm before it surfaces, the delayed setup of the Burrower strike package collapses and leaves too little left to trade with.
843: Built around Norn Emissaries, Neurotyrants, Neurolictors, Maleceptors, Norn Assimilators, Biovores, and Zoanthropes, this is a high-synapse, multi-threat toolkit that flexes its Synaptic Imperatives round-by-round to shift the entire army's combat profile on demand. The win condition is presence and attrition — Neurolictors and Norn Emissaries contest midboard while Biovores chip screening units and Maleceptors threaten armour, letting each turn's chosen Imperative amplify whichever arm of the army is doing the heavy lifting. It punishes slower gunlines that can't simultaneously answer mobile monsters at range and aggressive synapse units in their face, spreading anti-tank resources thin against multiple independent threats. However, it struggles against lists with consistent high-AP volume fire that can efficiently remove its expensive synapse pieces, collapsing the Imperative engine before it generates enough tempo to close out the game.
851: Built around Kroot Carnivores, Krootox Riders, Krootox Rampagers, and Kroot Lone-Spears flooding the board alongside Pathfinder Teams and Stealth Battlesuits, this is a mass-horde midtable brawler that drowns opponents in Kroot bodies while maintaining mobile anti-armour threats. The core engine is the Kroot Hunting Pack's escalating hit-and-wound bonus — once units are chipped below Starting Strength or half-strength, the Kroot swarm punishes them exponentially harder, so the plan is to trade efficiently early, trigger the damage amplifiers, and grind through the mid-game scoring window. It excels against hordes and medium infantry that struggle to wipe entire Kroot blobs cleanly, leaving damaged units exposed to the double-trigger kill chain. High-volume mortal wound output and elite alpha-strike lists that delete entire units in a single activation short-circuit the mechanic entirely, denying the below-strength conditions the army depends on.
853:
Built around Defilers, Cultist Mobs, and Vashtorr the Arkifane, this Cabal of Chaos list uses Dark Pacts to supercharge its daemon vehicles into a mobile anti-armour and midfield brawling force, with cultists flooding objectives as cheap screens and action monkeys.

The win condition is forcing opponents to deal with multiple threatening Defilers and Vashtorr simultaneously — Dark Pact-boosted shooting strips heavy targets while the daemon engines crash into the midfield and contest with superior volume of attacks, leaving cultists to quietly bank secondaries.

It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't efficiently answer multiple durable, self-buffing vehicles across the whole board on the same turn.

Hordes and high-volume anti-vehicle lists crack it open, as Defilers are vulnerable to anti-tank overload and the cultist screens fold quickly to mass firepower, leaving the daemon engines exposed without bodies to hide behind.
856: Built around Spiritseers, Wraithlords, Wraithguard, Wraithblades, and Farseer Skyrunners, this is a durable Wraith-heavy force running the Spirit Conclave detachment to turn its own psychic deaths into offensive fuel — enemy units that destroy Asuryani Psykers accumulate Vengeful Dead tokens, after which every Wraith Construct swings with +1 to hit and +1 to wound against that target. The plan is to bait out kills on cheap Spiritseers, then avalanche buffed Wraithguard and Wraithblades into the now-marked unit to grind it off the board while Wraithlords hold mid-table objectives. It punishes armies that commit to focused psychic-first removal, converting that aggression directly into a kill chain that rewards the opponent for doing exactly what they need to do. However, opponents who ignore the Psykers entirely — or who can clear the Wraith Constructs at range before the token engine activates — sidestep the core mechanic and leave this list sluggish and outscored.
863: Built around Darnath Lysander, Terminator Assault Squads, standard Terminator Squads, a Librarian in Terminator Armour, Bladeguard Veterans, and Intercessors, this Emperor's Shield list is a heavily armoured mid-table press that advances a dense wall of 2+ save infantry toward the opponent's deployment zone. 929: Built around Gaunt's Ghosts, Tempestus Scions, Krieg Combat Engineers, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Scout Sentinels, Cadian Shock Troops, Cadian Command Squads, Cadian Recon Squads, Cadian Castellans, and Kasrkin, this is a mass-infantry gunline that floods the board with bodies and layered ranged threats under Designation Force, using the designation mechanic to extend detection range and strip cover from priority targets. The win condition is volume-of-fire attrition — stacking command buffs and elite Scion drops to delete key enemy pieces while cheap infantry chaff buries objectives under sheer model count. It punishes low-model elite armies that struggle to clear screens efficiently, grinding them down through mobile anti-armour pressure from Sentinels and Engineers while the horde locks up midfield. It cracks open against fast, high-damage armies that can shatter the screening layers before the gunline stabilises, since the build's staying power depends on keeping bodies between the guns and the enemy.
2740: Built around massed Crusader Squads, Assault Intercessors, and Intercessors led by Helbrecht, the Emperor's Champion, Chaplain Grimaldus, and a swarm of Marshals and Lieutenants inside Bastion Task Force, this is a body-count castle that floods the board with cheap, character-buffed infantry and Repulsor Executioners providing heavy fire support. The engine is volume: Battleline units that can shoot and charge after Advancing or Falling Back stay glued to objectives while still threatening kills, letting the list score primary through sheer presence and secondary through attrition rather than dedicated strike packages. It punishes horde and mid-range gunline armies that struggle to chew through layered bodies quickly enough, as the stack of leader buffs and Blades of Valour keep the blob fighting well above its points cost. Concentrated elite shooting or high-damage melee — anything that deletes whole combat squads in a single activation — cracks the castle open, because once the body count drops the scoring engine stalls and the list has no fast repositioning tool to recover contested zones.
2728: Built around Skarbrand, Be'lakor, a Great Unclean One, a Lord of Change, and screening bodies in Plaguebearers, Beasts of Nurgle, and Flesh Hounds, this is a mixed-god Daemonic Incursion list that deploys a murderer's row of Greater Daemons supported by cheap, durable chaff. The plan is to use the detachment's deep strike rule to land threats precisely within the Shadow of Chaos or hugging a Greater Daemon's bubble, threatening multiple angles simultaneously while the screen-and-deny infantry holds objectives and bleeds opponents dry. It punishes mid-range combat armies that can't handle simultaneous threats at different threat levels, as layered lethality from multiple Greater Daemons with different damage profiles overwhelms single-axis defensive lists. However, elite shooting armies that can sequentially delete Greater Daemons before they land or fight back crack this list open, since losing even one anchor piece collapses the deep strike threat network.
2726: Built around Plaguebearers, Great Unclean Ones, Rotigus, Beasts of Nurgle, and Nurglings, supported by Sloppity Bilepipers, Poxbringers, and Skull Cannons, this is a slow-rolling Plague Legion tide that uses Warptide to advance Battleline units and still charge, keeping relentless pressure across the midboard. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that struggle to stay out of the 9" Shadow of Chaos bubble and can't trade efficiently into masses of Lethal Hits. High-mobility armies that can keep distance, contest objectives from range, and avoid clustering inside the aura will bleed it dry before it ever gets its grinding engine running.
2725: Built around Bloodcrushers (typically two squads), Flesh Hounds, Rendmasters on Blood Throne, Bloodthirsters, and Be'lakor, this is a fast Khorne-heavy cavalry list running the Cavalcade of Chaos detachment — every mounted unit that falls back can still shoot and charge, turning retreating into a form of aggressive repositioning. The win condition is layered threat saturation: Bloodcrushers and Bloodthirsters crack armor while Be'lakor with Fade to Darkness provides character support and psychological pressure, forcing opponents to over-commit resources to stopping whichever hammer arrives first. It punishes static gunlines and elite low-model armies that can't handle multiple independent charges per turn across a wide frontage. It struggles against high-volume mortal wound output or screens deep enough to deny charge lanes, since the entire engine depends on getting mounted units into combat without being whittled apart in the approach.
2727: Built around a Bloodthirster, Be'lakor, one or two Lords of Change, Flesh Hounds, Cultist Mob, and Beasts of Nurgle, this Shadow Legion force is a high-mobility toolbox that floods the board with threats across all four Chaos gods. The win condition is threat saturation — Bloodthirster and Flesh Hounds crash forward as kill-pieces while Be'lakor and the Lords of Change project board control and layered lethality, with Warptide (in 70% of lists) letting Battleline units advance and still charge, turning objective repositions into surprise threat deliveries. It punishes gunline armies that can't handle simultaneous melee and psychic pressure from multiple angles, stripping screens with horde bodies then crashing elite killers into exposed backfield units. The weakness is durability variance — this build has no single resilient anchor, and lists that can isolate and delete its key pieces one at a time before they all land in the same turn will crack it open.
2729: Built around Lords of Changes and Plaguebearers, this list pairs high-mobility, high-output psyker monsters with durable, objective-squatting infantry under the Lords of the Warp detachment, whose CHARACTER buff gives non-monster characters improved Leadership and OC. The win condition is board control through attrition: Lords of Change project ranged and melee threat across multiple vectors while Plaguebearers camp scoring zones and dare opponents to commit resources to clear them. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to simultaneously contest objectives and answer multiple dangerous monsters. It cracks open against mechanised or shooting-heavy lists that can delete Lords of Change before they cycle damage, leaving the slow Plaguebearer core isolated and unable to score independently.
2703: Built around Defilers, Noise Marines, Chaos Bikers, Chosen riding Chaos Rhinos, and Huron Blackheart commanding Red Corsairs Raiders, this is an aggressive mid-board brawler that hits across every threat category simultaneously. The detachment's twin payoffs do the heavy lifting: Heretic Astartes ranged weapons gain Assault to fire on the move, then punish any unit sitting on an objective with an automatic AP improvement — meaning contested markers become kill zones where this army wins every trade. Rhino-mounted Chosen and mobile Bikers apply constant pressure across the table, while Defilers and Noise Marines layer anti-armour and volume fire to overload defensive screens. It cracks open armies that rely on fragile objective holders, but struggles against opponents who can strip transports at range before the assault element closes.
2706: Built around Chosen, Possessed, Cultist Mobs, Legionaries, Mutilators, and Masters of the Maelstrom — all buffed by Fabius Bile's Creations of Bile augmentations — this is a mass-horde infantry army that floods the board with enhanced Heretic Astartes, selecting or rolling for augmentations at battle start to stack buffs across multiple infantry units simultaneously. The win condition is body-count attrition: cheap Cultists screen and hold while augmented Chosen and Possessed grind through mid-table brawls, with Mutilators dropping in as late-game closers to contest or steal objectives. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear waves of infantry and cannot trade efficiently into expendable screens backed by buffed combat units. It cracks open against armies that can strip the augmentation value early through precision mortal wound output or long-range firepower that bypasses the screen before the mid-table brawl ever begins.
2739: Built around cultist mobs screening objectives and War Dog Karnivores hunting armoured targets, this list folds Chaos Space Marines DAMNED infantry into a Chaos Knights chassis via the Iconoclast Fiefdom detachment, blending expendable bodies with fast, hard-hitting war engines across a wide variety of big Knights and War Dog variants. The plan is to use cultists as a cheap, durable screen that holds ground and absorbs early pressure while Karnivores and supporting War Dogs tear through opposing vehicles and monsters, generating scoring opportunities through board control rather than passive sitting. It punishes mechanised and armour-heavy lists brutally — the mobile anti-armour toolkit means tank lines get dismantled fast, and cultist screens deny easy early charges into the Knights themselves. Where it cracks is against elite infantry-dense armies that can trade efficiently into cultists and then isolate individual Knights, particularly when anti-armour overload isn't needed and the enemy can simply out-score on naked objectives.
2704: Built around Defilers, Obliterators, Mutilators, Warpsmiths, and Cultist Mobs, this Devotees of Destruction list plays a brutally physical mid-table game — heavy daemon engines brawling for space while Obliterators' HEAVY-boosted ranged attacks punish anything that tries to hold distance. The plan is to bully the midfield with Mutilators and Defilers grinding through opposing units while Obliterators methodically delete armoured threats from stationary firing positions, accumulating board control and secondary leverage. It punishes mechanised and elite-armour lists hard, combining anti-tank overload from multiple Obliterator squads with melee pressure that forces opponents into no-win positioning. It struggles against fast objective-denial armies that can isolate and overwhelm individual daemon engines before the Warpsmiths can sustain them, and its below-average win rate signals vulnerability to anything that outranges or screens the midfield push effectively.
2705: Built around Fabius Bile, Kravek Morne, Chaos Terminators, Possessed, Mutilators, and waves of Cultists and Legionaries operating under the Creations of Bile detachment, this is a melee-forward horde army that uses augmentation buffs to punch well above its points cost across a mass of Heretic Astartes Infantry. The plan is to flood the mid-table with durable, buffed bodies — Possessed and Mutilators doing the heavy brawling while Cultists screen and contest objectives — letting Bile's augmentation selection tailor the threat profile to whatever the opponent brings. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear volume, as sheer body count combined with augmented melee output creates an anti-tank and anti-elite overload across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. It cracks open when faced with high-volume mortal wounds or mass-blast firepower that bypasses toughness buffs, and its relatively slow movement means a disciplined opponent can screen their backfield and deny the brawl entirely.
2708: Built around Obliterators, Havocs, Legionaries, Cultist Mobs, and Chaos Rhinos under the Devotees of Destruction detachment, this list plays a grinding mid-board gunline backed by massed infantry — Obliterators and Havocs gain Heavy on all ranged attacks, rewarding static positioning and punishing lists that let them stand still. The plan is to hold objectives with Cultists and Rhino-mounted Legionaries while Obliterators and Havocs pour sustained Heavy fire into priority targets, chipping armour and elite infantry down through sheer volume before moving to score. It punishes lightly screened elite armies and slow armoured lists that can't quickly dislodge the gunline before it gains the Heavy bonus and starts hitting more reliably. Fast alpha-strike lists and mobile deep-strike threats crack it open by forcing the Obliterators and Havocs to reposition, stripping the Heavy bonus and disrupting the scoring infantry before they can anchor the midboard.
541: Built around Raptors, Warp Talons, a jump pack Chaos Lord, Obliterators, and Cultist Mob screens, this is a Murdertalon Raiders list that leverages its detachment's hit-reroll engine against weakened and battle-shocked enemies to punish anything it can soften first. The win condition is a compounding pressure loop: Obliterators crack armour and force casualties, pushing units below half-strength, then the airborne assault elements pile in with re-rolling hits against those degraded targets while Cultists flood objectives. It punishes elite low-model-count armies especially hard, since a single casualty can trigger the half-strength threshold and flip both offensive and defensive bonuses simultaneously. Armies with durable high-toughness bricks that resist attrition — particularly multi-wound vehicle spam — can stall the degradation engine before the re-roll conditions ever activate.
650: Built around Cultist Mobs, Chaos Rhinos, Legionaries, Chosen, and Obliterators, this list floods the table with cheap bodies and mid-tier infantry while Obliterators provide a roving heavy-weapons platform that can threaten armour from nearly anywhere. The plan is to smother objectives with expendable Cultist screens, grind through the midfield with Legionaries and Chosen hitting close, and let Obliterators punish anything valuable that pokes out of cover. It particularly punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't clear waves of cheap bodies fast enough to contest primary scoring. However, lists that can efficiently delete Cultist chaff at range and then isolate the Obliterators — leaving the mid-tier infantry unsupported — will crack this build open before its grinding attrition engine gets traction.
2707: Built around Chosen, Cultist Mobs screened forward in Chaos Rhinos, and Abaddon the Despoiler anchoring the melee threat, this is a combined-arms Chaos Space Marines list that blends a genuine horde presence with mobile anti-armour and a punishing close-combat centrepiece. The gameplan is to flood mid-table objectives with expendable Cultists and Rhino-delivered Chosen while Abaddon crashes into the opponent's most dangerous unit, using his raw hitting power to rip apart elite targets and free up the rest of the army to score. Against low-model-count elite armies this list punishes economically, overwhelming priority targets with volume attacks from Cultists and Chosen while Abaddon and supporting armour — Predator Destructors and Forgefiends appearing in roughly a third of lists — deny parking space. Concentrated high-damage output from heavy-shooting factions can strip the Rhinos early and leave Chosen exposed on approach, and without a consistent detachment identity the list lacks the focused mechanical synergy to compensate when the delivery mechanism dies.
2702: Built around Lion El'Jonson, Azrael, Ravenwing Command Squads, Land Speeder Vengances, Sammael, Scout Squads, and Ravenwing Black Knights, this is a fast, multi-threat Dark Angels force that blends biker shock troops with hard-hitting skimmer fire support. The plan is to use Scouts to pre-screen objectives while the bike elements race forward to contest and punish exposed units, with the Land Speeder Vengances providing sustained heavy firepower that forces opponents to respond on two axes simultaneously. It punishes slower, static gunlines that can't reposition to handle both the mobile biker pressure and the skimmer overwatch, getting torn apart trying to prioritize targets. It cracks open against armies that can strip the fast movers early with high-volume anti-armour or precise anti-mounted shooting, leaving the list without the mobile leverage it depends on to threaten the whole board.
2700: Built around Land Speeder Vengances, Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, and Sammael as the aerial fire platform, supported by Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Inner Circle Companions, and Outriders providing melee teeth and objective muscle, the entire list runs Darkflight Pursuit — granting every RAVENWING FLY unit Ignores Cover on ranged attacks. The plan is to park a wall of fast-moving skimmers that strip cover saves from entrenched infantry and armour alike, while Companions and Outriders apply melee pressure to force opponents off objectives and create scoring lanes. It punishes static gunlines and cover-dependent armies hardest, denying the defensive benefit those builds rely on while projecting mobile anti-armour fire across the table. Aggressive deep-strike or alpha-strike lists that close the distance fast expose its relative fragility before the skimmer screen can reposition.
2693: Built around Mortarion, Deathshroud Terminators, a Daemon Prince of Nurgle, Defilers, a Lord of Contagion, a Tallyman, and Poxwalkers flooding objectives, this list runs Virulent Vectorium to turn every controlled objective into a persistent threat — enemies within range become Afflicted, creating layered attrition pressure across the entire board. The win condition is objective lockdown: plant Poxwalkers on points, trigger the Afflicted condition through the detachment rule, and let Mortarion and the Deathshroud clean up anything durable enough to contest. It punishes elite low-model-count lists brutally, as Afflicted attrition stacks fastest against armies that can't afford to lose individual models contesting objectives. Armies with high-mobility deep strike threats or strong alpha-strike output can bypass the screen and remove Mortarion before the attritional engine gets rolling.
2694: Built around Defilers, Poxwalkers, and Mortarion, this list uses the Mortarion's Hammer detachment to tag priority enemy units with Afflicted each battle round from range, layering contagion pressure across the table while Defilers provide mobile anti-armour punch and Poxwalkers clog objectives. The win condition is attrition through stacked lethality — Afflicted units take degraded combat effectiveness while Mortarion and the Defilers hunt armour, and Poxwalkers absorb casualties to hold ground. It punishes slow, durable armies that cluster beyond 12", where the Afflicted mechanic reaches its peak efficiency and the Defilers' mobility finds isolated targets. Armies that can alpha-strike Mortarion or screen tightly enough to deny the 12" Afflicted window crack this list open, since its engine collapses without reliable target selection at range.
2701: Built around Azrael, multiple Land Speeder Vengeances, Ravenwing Black Knights, Hellblasters, and a Lieutenant, this Dark Age Arsenal list turns plasma into the army's primary kill tool by boosting every plasma weapon's Strength by 1 across the board. The plan is to park high-volume plasma output behind Azrael's invulnerable aura, use the Black Knights and Speeders to threaten flanks and maintain board pressure, and grind through mid-tier armour and elite infantry that can't trade efficiently against sustained plasma volume. It punishes armies relying on medium-wound-count elites and low-save infantry that fold to supercharged plasma saturation. However, it struggles against heavy-armour spam and aggressive alpha-strike lists that can bypass or collapse Azrael's bubble before the gunline finds its footing.
2709: Built around Talos pain engines, Cronos parasites, massed Venoms, Scourges with heavy weapons, Incubi, Mandrakes, Wracks, and an Archon-Haemonculus-Drazhar command suite, this is a layered Drukhari combined-arms swarm that floods the board across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally, as the sheer number of independent threats stretching across skimmer fire, monstrous melee, and deep-striking Scourge anti-armour creates an impossible triage problem. Concentrated high-AP shooting or anything that strips Venoms in turn one collapses the delivery system and leaves infantry dangerously exposed before they can engage.
2710:
Built around Ravagers, Venoms, Raiders, Archons, Incubi, Wyches, Kabalite Warriors, Reavers, Mandrakes, Scourges, Lady Malys, and Drazhar, this is a full-spectrum Dark Eldar skimmer swarm that floods the board with fast transports, elite melee, and layered ranged pressure across multiple detachment configurations.

The win condition is simultaneous threat overload — Ravagers strip armour from range while Venoms and Raiders deliver Incubi and Wyches into melee, forcing opponents to answer anti-tank and elite infantry threats in the same turn they need to hold objectives.

It punishes armies that rely on one defensive answer, since the triple threat of skimmer fire, transport-delivered melee, and Scourge heavy weapons demands multiple counter-strategies at once.

It cracks open against boards that can shut down movement and screen aggressively, since the list's lethality depends on precise positioning of fragile, low-wound vehicles that collapse quickly under sustained focused fire.
2699: Built around Hyperadapted Raveners, Purestrain Genestealers, Von Ryan's Leapers, and Achilles Ridgerunners flooding the board alongside a dense screen of Neophyte Hybrids and Acolyte Hybrids, this list fuses Genestealer Cult bodies with Tyranid Vanguard Invader units under Final Day's alliance rule, creating one of the most numerically overwhelming mid-board brawling armies in the game. The plan is to drown opponents in bodies, contest every objective with expendable Neophyte screens healing back wounds in terrain through Xenocult Masses, while Raveners and Purestrains delete anything that steps forward to clear them. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't efficiently trade into 20+ activations, running out of damage before the cult runs out of threats. Armies with reliable board-wide blast or mortal-wound output can systematically strip the horde faster than Xenocult Masses can patch it, cracking open the scoring engine before the brawlers close the gap.
2698: Built around Hybrid Metamorphs, Acolyte Hybrids, Purestrain Genestealers, Neophyte Hybrids, Biophagus, Acolyte Iconward, Goliath Trucks, Achilles Ridgerunners, Reductus Saboteur, Benefictus, and Atalan Jackals, this is a mass-horde assault list running Xenocreed Congregation to fuel re-roll Advance and Charge rolls on character-led infantry, with Iconwards and Magi soaking wounds on FNP 3+ while leading units. The plan is to flood the midboard with waves of close-combat infantry delivered by Goliath Trucks, threatening multi-unit charges every turn while Ridgerunners provide mobile anti-armour pressure and the Neophyte blobs terrain-anchor for the Xenocult Masses heal. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot generate enough high-quality overwatch or board control to stop three or more simultaneous charge threats crashing in with re-rolls. It struggles against high-volume mortal wound output or strong shooting armies that can gut the transport layer before the Trucks deliver their cargo, leaving expensive melee units stranded short.
2743: Built around multiple Knight Destriers averaging over two per list, this is a fast, armour-cracking force that leans into mobility as its primary weapon rather than static gunlines. The engine is simple: advance aggressively with heavily armed Knights, applying relentless anti-armour pressure across multiple threat vectors simultaneously to overwhelm opponents who cannot prioritise targets fast enough. It punishes lists that concentrate high-toughness vehicles into a single kill-zone, because two-plus Destriers force awkward target prioritisation while still contesting objectives across the board. The weakness is durability — without a consistent detachment providing defensive tech across all lists, a coordinated alpha strike that cripples one or two Destriers early collapses the threat density the entire plan depends on.
2717: Built around Subductor Squads, Imperial Navy Breachers, Sisters of Battle in Immolators, Grey Knights Terminators, and a constellation of Inquisitors, Assassins, and Navigators operating across both Veiled Blade Elimination Force and Imperialis Fleet detachments, this is a transport-heavy horde that floods the board with cheap, durable infantry bodies. It punishes static gunlines and elite low-model-count armies that can't contest the sheer number of scoring threats simultaneously. It cracks open against anything that deletes transports efficiently, stranding infantry in the open and collapsing the board presence the entire scoring plan depends on.
2718: Built around Deathwatch Kill Teams, Subductor Squads, Watch Masters, Imperial Navy Breachers, and a dense supporting cast of Inquisitors, Navigators, Rhinos, and Assassins operating under Imperialis Fleet and Veiled Blade Elimination Force, this is a mass-infantry gunline that floods the board with bodies across multiple force-org keywords. The win condition is applying Eliminate At All Costs to a priority threat each Command phase while Assassins burn their doubled-up Overkill, Soulless Horror, and Shieldbreaker abilities to strip key pieces, all while transports and Breachers grind objectives under sheer volume of fire. It punishes low-model-count elite armies mercilessly — the combination of skimmer-mounted firepower, layered lethal hits, and constant designation pressure overwhelms lists that cannot absorb attritional trade across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. However, coordinated alpha strikes or armies that can isolate and delete the Watch Masters early disrupt the designation engine before it spins up, and the build's reliance on keyword soup over durable synergy leaves it vulnerable to efficient, high-damage shooting that ignores bodies.
2742: Built around the Knight Crusader, Knight Castellan, and Cerastus Knight Atrapos, this list uses the Dominus Foebreakers detachment to punish enemies sheltering in terrain, adding +1 to hit rolls against anything hiding in cover and turning defensive positioning into a liability. The win condition is straightforward anti-armour overload: park the Castellan and Crusader in advantageous lanes, delete high-value targets with massed heavy firepower each turn, and use the Atrapos as a mobile threat piece that closes distance and tears apart armoured units in melee or at range. Archeotech Autoloaders, taken in nearly three-quarters of lists, amplifies output further, and the build ruthlessly punishes elite armoured lists that cannot spread wounds or hide effectively. Cheap, expendable screening units are the counter — anything that floods the midboard with bodies forces awkward targeting choices and can bog down Knights in combat before the big guns can clear lanes.
546: Built around the Void Dragon, the Nightbringer, and Immortals under the Hand of the Dynasty detachment, this list fields multiple C'tan Shards as its hammers while Immortals with the Assault rule on their ranged weapons provide mobile, action-safe scoring bodies. The win condition is threat saturation — deploying two or more unchallengeable combat monsters forces the opponent into impossible trade decisions while Immortals advance and action freely without sacrificing shooting. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot generate enough quality attacks to simultaneously down multiple Shards before being ground apart in melee. However, it cracks against high-volume mid-strength firepower that efficiently chips Shards and exploits the list's limited redundancy in scoring infantry, leaving objectives exposed when the big monsters get pinned into combat.
2716: Built around the Void Dragon, Nightbringer, Deceiver, and Transcendent C'tan as the primary threats, with Ophydian Destroyers, Flayed Ones, Tomb Blades, and Lokhust Heavy Destroyers providing supporting firepower and board presence, all operating under Hypercrypt Legion with most lists also running Skyshroud Spearhead. The plan is to use Hypercrypt's end-of-turn repositioning to teleport C'tan and key units into ideal strike positions each round, while Tomb Blades deep strike in and shoot with +1 to hit, applying lethal pressure from multiple vectors simultaneously. This build punishes slower, castle-style armies that rely on static positioning, since the constant teleportation makes threat angles nearly impossible to screen against. It cracks open when faced with armies that can project consistent high-damage output into multiple large targets at once, as losing even one C'tan early dramatically collapses the pressure network.
2744: Built around one or more Stompas supported by Gretchin screens, Meks keeping the big walkers repaired, and Boyz providing midfield bodies, this list leans hard into Dread Mob in two-thirds of lists — a detachment that lets ORKS WALKER units roll variable dice to gain special rules when attacking, at the risk of a hazard roll when pushing hardest. The plan is to crash Stompas into the midboard, leverage their layered lethality to delete anything they touch, and use Gretchin and Boyz to screen objectives while the Meks sustain the centrepiece. It punishes lists that lack dedicated anti-titanic firepower by simply absorbing moderate damage and grinding forward with mass bodies and Walker attacks. However, concentrated high-volume anti-tank or mortal wound output that can disable a Stompa early collapses the entire threat engine before the list can generate value.
833: Built around Scout Squads, Intercessor Squads, and Repulsor Executioners, this is a gunline-anchored combined-arms force that layers cheap, durable infantry screens in front of heavy armoured firepower. The Repulsor Executioners do the heavy lifting, pushing mobile anti-armour and high-volume fire from behind a wall of bodies while infantry hold primary objectives and bleed opponents off secondaries. It punishes slow, high-toughness armies that want to close the gap, overloading their durability with sustained tank fire before they can ever reach the backline. However, fast aggression and alpha-strike pressure crack it open early — if the screens evaporate before the Executioners can cycle their guns, the list has no meaningful answer to being overrun at close range.
2738: Built around Terminator Squads, Librarians in Terminator Armour, and Intercessor Squads, this list leans heavily on a psyker-driven heavy gunline, cycling Psychic Disciplines each battle round to buff the entire force — Divination for hit/wound re-rolls, Pyromancy for ranged pressure, or Biomancy for unexpected aggression. The win condition is grinding attrition from midfield: Terminators hold anchoring positions under a rotating discipline umbrella while Intercessors screen and score, turning sustained firepower into points through kill efficiency and objective denial. It punishes lists that rely on incremental damage output, since the Librarius Conclave's discipline rotation lets the army adapt its re-roll economy to whichever threat axis the opponent leans on hardest. However, fast alpha-strike armies that can isolate and overwhelm individual Terminator bricks before disciplines resolve will crack this list open, as the build's moderate mobility leaves it vulnerable to being out-positioned early.
2733:
Built around the Land Raider Redeemer, Bladeguard Veterans, Intercessors, and Scout Squads, this list presents a heavy armoured fist with durable infantry riding shotgun.

The plan is to push the Redeemer into mid-board, using Scouts to screen and deny early objective pressure while Bladeguard Veterans threaten brutal close-range punishments, letting the army grind out primary scoring behind an armoured wall.

It punishes slower, infantry-heavy armies that can't efficiently answer both a T8 transport and a wave of durable 2+ save melee elites simultaneously, forcing opponent resources to split across multiple hard targets.

Where it struggles is against high-volume anti-tank or melta overload lists that can delete the Redeemer early, collapsing the delivery system before the melee core ever engages.
2734: Built around Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Hammerstrikes, Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, Intercessors, and Scouts, this Fulguris Task Force list opens with an aggressive first-turn ingress move, deploying its SPEEDER units deep into the midfield or flanks before the opponent can react. The win condition is anti-armour overload at range combined with mobile infantry pressure — Speeders and Hammerstrikes hammer heavy targets while jump pack Intercessors and Scouts screen objectives and contest secondaries. It punishes slow, static gunlines that can't reposition, since the turn-one ingress floods the board before castle-style lists can establish fire lanes. However, concentrated alpha-strike lists that can strip the exposed Speeders in response — or elite melee forces that can hunt the lighter infantry screen — will crack it open, as the build lacks the durability to absorb sustained punishment after its opening gambit.
2735: Built around Marneus Calgar with Victrix Honour Guard keeping him alive, Bladeguard Veterans, Vanguard Veterans and Assault Intercessors with jump packs, and a dense screen of Scouts and Intercessors, this is a melee-dominant objective army running the Reclamation Force detachment. It punishes armies that trade melee into objective-holding blobs, as the AP improvement and defensive trigger stack to make contested objectives genuinely costly for the opponent. It struggles against ranged pressure that can deny objective control before the phase begins, collapsing the defensive trigger and leaving its elite melee units exposed without the durability bonus they depend on.
2731: Built around multiple Librarians cycling Psychic Disciplines each battle round, Bladeguard Veterans as a close-combat hammer, and Intercessors and Scouts holding ground across the midfield, this Librarius Conclave list plays as a flexible, psyker-amplified gunline with meaningful melee teeth. The engine is the Disciplines system itself — every round the list picks between a movement buff, re-rolling hits and wounds of 1, or enhanced ranged output across all Adeptus Astartes Psyker units, tuning its damage profile to the immediate threat and grinding opponents off objectives through sustained efficiency rather than a single explosive turn. It punishes slower gunline armies that can't withstand round-over-round re-roll stacking and consistent volume fire, particularly when Scouts deny forward positions and Bladeguard lock down key units in melee. 2737: Built around Aethon Shaan, Inceptor Squads, Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, Kayvaan Shrike, Vanguard Veterans with Jump Packs, Centurion Devastators, Incursors, and Scouts, this list runs the Shadowmark Talon detachment, exploiting its passive cover save on all ranged attacks beyond 12" to make the entire army stubbornly hard to shoot off objectives.
